_comment: THE MANAGER'S ONE REGISTER. Adopted 2026-09-21 (operator-directed operating reset).
Scope of record: docs/plans/OPERATING-PLAN-2026-09-21.md. Manager contract: .claude/skills/manager/SKILL.md.
The previous 323-row file is preserved verbatim at
RULES FOR THIS FILE, because the last one grew 67 top-level keys and 323 rows:
1. items[] is the content. Top-level keys are schema only - no narrative,
no timestamped manager_observation_* / manager_tick_* entries, no incident logs.
Three observations an hour apart on one row is the failure mode, not diligence.
2. ONE status field: `state`, from the `states` vocabulary below. There is no `status`.
3. `done` and `landed_unproven` are DIFFERENT FACTS and are never collapsed.
4. A row that is neither a plan item nor a live lane does not belong here.
A question goes to research/queue/<id>.yaml instead.
5. This file is served to the operator as the live Workflow page via
GET /api/bot/work/checklist, read from the VM's working tree. ict-git-sync
pulls main every ~5 min, so the page is as fresh as the last push TO MAIN.
cycle_intent: Make the promotion ladder mechanical and the research loop terminate in a decision. Edge is decided offline; a book only ever checks mechanics and cost.

states.queued: scoped and agreed, nobody started it
states.in_flight: a lane is actively working it
states.blocked: waiting on the typed edge(s) in blocked_on
states.dropped: deliberately not doing; note says why

item_schema.id: plan item id (A1..D3) or a lane id
item_schema.title: one line
item_schema.lane: session id once dispatched, else null
item_schema.model: the model chosen for the lane, with the reason in `note`
item_schema.ceiling_usd: per-lane dollar ceiling; on breach READ what it produced, then kill or re-scope
item_schema.spend_usd: actual, filled in by the cost meter (A1)
item_schema.tier: 1 | 2 | 3 - the approval the resulting change needs
item_schema.blocked_on: typed edges [{kind, ref, what}] — kind is `work_item` or `operator_decision`, ref names the blocker, what says why. Empty list = nothing declared blocks it.
item_schema.note: what is true about this row. Not a log.

items.title: Cost meter — usage against the WEEKLY PLAN ALLOWANCE, plus per-lane dollars
items.note: OPERATOR DECISION 2026-09-21: 'pace ourselves based on the weekly budget for the $200 Max plan -- 10% of the weekly budget a day, so we leave a wide margin for error or unexpected needs.' 10%/day x 7 = 70% of the weekly allowance, 30% margin. [!] THIS CHANGES WHAT THIS ITEM MEASURES AND THE CHANGE IS NOT COSMETIC. A subscription plan's constraint is a WEEKLY USAGE ALLOWANCE, not a dollar spend. Every cost_usd figure in the plan (the $125 across two resumed lanes, the $11.88 in ten minutes) is API-EQUIVALENT PRICING read off session metadata -- the right signal for COMPARING lanes, the wrong denominator for PACING against a plan. Report usage-against-allowance as the budget line, keep dollars beside it as the per-lane comparison. [!] THE DENOMINATOR IS NOT ESTABLISHED AND MUST NOT BE INVENTED: the exact weekly allowance is not readable from this repo. FIRST JOB is to establish it from whatever surface reports plan usage, or from the operator, and to report `unknown` rather than substitute a figure until it has. A fabricated denominator under a real rule is worse than no meter. [!] THE DENOMINATOR IS ESTABLISHED 2026-09-21, AND IT IS A PERCENTAGE, NOT A TOKEN COUNT. The operator read Settings > Usage directly. Plan: Max (20x). The surface exposes THREE meters, each a percent-of-allowance bar with no absolute number anywhere: a ~5-hour SESSION window, a WEEKLY window, and a SEPARATE WEEKLY LIMIT FOR FABLE. Anthropic's own support pages publish no figure either -- only '20x Pro per-session allowance'. [!] DO NOT CONVERT TO TOKENS, and this is a design decision rather than a limitation. The allowance is MODEL-WEIGHTED, so tokens-per-percent is not a constant -- it is a function of the model mix and moves whenever the manager routes a lane to sonnet instead of opus. A token budget would read as precise and drift silently. A1 METERS IN PERCENT. The operator's rule -- 10% of the weekly budget per day -- is already stated in that unit, so no conversion is needed to enforce it. A measured per-model exchange rate may be reported as a sanity check, labelled measured and drifting, NEVER as the budget. [!] TWO WINDOWS BIND, NOT ONE. The weekly cap is what the 10%/day rule governs; the ~5-hour session window is what actually walls a lane mid-run. A day's 10% spent as a single burst can exhaust the session window while the weekly meter still reads green, so A1 MUST SHOW BOTH or it reports 'fine' during an outage. [!] MEASURED 2026-09-21, and it CORRECTS an earlier claim on this row that was asserted rather than checked. The claim was that a meter summing only agent lanes would systematically under-report because the operator's own chat draws on the same pool. The mechanism is real -- all surfaces do share one limit -- but the magnitude is currently ZERO: 'What's using your week' reads Claude Code 100%, Chats 0%, Cowork 0%, Other 0%. Lane accounting is therefore ~= the whole pool today. A1 should still LABEL its scope, because the day that mix changes the meter goes quietly wrong. [!] THE MANAGER'S METER IS THE **DAILY** BUDGET, NOT THE WEEKLY BAR (operator, 2026-09-21): 'the manager should be focused on the daily budget, not weekly, as I sometimes use Claude for other projects... I will start a new manager session after this one and I expect it to use the daily budget, even if we pass into the margin.' [!] THIS CORRECTS A CLAIM WRITTEN ON THIS ROW EARLIER THE SAME DAY, and it is the SAME CATEGORY ERROR this row already caught once with cost_usd. That claim read: '68% of the week consumed with ~2 of 7 days left, ~13.6%/day against a 10%/day target, so THE STATED POLICY IS NOT BEING MET.' It compared TOTAL weekly consumption against the MANAGER'S daily allowance -- two different populations. The weekly bar aggregates every surface and every project the operator touches, including work this repo's manager cannot see and did not cause, so it CANNOT grade the manager. ('Claude Code 100%' does not rescue it: the operator's other projects are also Claude Code.) The 68% reading stands as a fact about the ACCOUNT; the conclusion drawn from it was unsupported and is withdrawn. [!] SO A1 REPORTS TWO DIFFERENT THINGS AND MUST NOT BLEND THEM. (a) THE CONTROL VARIABLE: this repo's spend today against the daily budget -- 10% of the weekly allowance. That is the number the manager is accountable for. (b) CONTEXT ONLY: the account-level weekly bar, unattributable and reported as such. A single blended 'budget' figure is the bug. [!] THE 30% WEEKLY MARGIN IS NOT A RESERVE THE MANAGER PRESERVES BY DOING LESS. It exists to absorb the operator's other projects and surprises. A manager that throttles its own lane because the ACCOUNT bar looks high is spending the margin's purpose on nothing. The operator has stated explicitly that the next manager should spend its daily budget EVEN IF that passes into the margin. [!] AND THE FAILURE MODE IS NOT HITTING A CAP -- it is 'losing work to sessions dying in the middle' (operator). THAT IS A DURABILITY PROBLEM, NOT A BUDGET ONE, and budgeting alone cannot fix it. The mitigations are structural: land work in small PRs rather than one large one, push before you answer, and keep state on disk (PIPELINE.jsonl, the checklist) rather than in a session's head. The ~5-HOUR SESSION WINDOW is what actually kills a session mid-task, so it is the in-session number to watch; the weekly bar never killed anything mid-run. [!] FABLE HAS A SEPARATE WEEKLY ALLOWANCE, MEASURED AT 0% USED, AND THE OPERATOR HAS DIRECTED THAT IT BE EMPLOYED (2026-09-21): 'it should definitely be used when appropriate -- we want to employ that budget as well, we just want to make sure it is getting the tasks that are the best use of that resource.' It is a SECOND pool that does not draw on the main one, so work routed there is additive capacity, not a trade-off. That makes it a live routing input for the model table in .claude/skills/manager/SKILL.md. Tracked as E11 -- A1 reports the pool, E11 decides what goes in it. [!] DISPATCHED 2026-09-21 alongside A3a rather than before it, because A3a was told to render section 5 WITHOUT the spend figures (it already has the unrouted count from pipeline.py) and to print an explicit 'not measured -- A1 not built' line. So the blocked_on edge is narrower than it read: section 5 ships either way and A1 fills it in. FRESH, sonnet-5. [!] THE QUESTION PUT TO THE LANE is deliberately not 'build a cost meter' but 'what does section 5 print on a day nobody has read the usage meter' -- because the denominator is not machine-readable and the failure mode on this row has twice been a figure that looked precise and was not. [!] BUILT 2026-09-21, PR #12683 open (draft, not merged -- state stays `in_flight` until the manager merges it; move to `landed_unproven` on merge, and `done` only once A3a's section-5 wiring is observed calling this module in a real brief): `scripts/ops/spend_meter.py` -- an append-only on-disk record of operator-entered readings (session/weekly/fable_weekly, percent + read_at) and `render_section_5()` for A3a to call. Verified this session: a day with no reading prints `never recorded` per window (never `0%`); a stale reading always renders its age and is never presented as current; per-lane `cost_usd` is reachable only from an interactive session holding `get_session`/`list_sessions` -- confirmed by calling those tools directly against this session and its parent manager -- and NOT from a CI runner or a Routine-fired turn (reconfirms, does not re-derive, the same finding already in `render_daily_brief.py` and `queue_latency.py`); no CI-reachable credential for it exists in this repo (checked: `.github/workflows/`, `docs/reference/env-vars.md`, `docs/claude/system-actions.md`). NOT yet wired into the real daily brief -- that is A3a's job, out of this row's scope fence. [!] MERGED 2026-09-21 as 9e9fb3a. ⚠️ SPEND CORRECTED 6.86 -> 28.03: the earlier figure was read MID-FLIGHT and left on the row looking like a total. A meter's own row reporting a stale number is the failure the meter exists to prevent. [!] ⚠️ SPEND CORRECTED AGAIN, READ AFTER ARCHIVING: $59.17. The figure committed hours earlier was ALSO mid-flight. [!] ⚠️ STATE CORRECTED BY THE LANE, NOT BY THE MANAGER (#12698): this row was marked `done` on the strength of #12683 merging, and the lane read origin/main:scripts/ops/render_daily_brief.py directly and found §5 STILL PRINTING `A1 (cost meter) is not built`. The meter is built, tested, guard-registered -- and nothing calls it. Merged is not deployed is not observed, and this row had collapsed the first into the third on the manager's say-so. [!] CLOSING THIS ROW MEANS: a real daily brief whose §5 prints a spend figure sourced from `spend_meter.render_section_5` -- not the placeholder `A1 (cost meter) is not built`, and not a hand-run of the module. The wiring is in `render_daily_brief.py`; re-reading `spend_meter.py` proves nothing, because the module was never the gap.

items.title: The follow-through pipeline — one intake, due conditions, and section 0 of the brief
items.note: OPERATOR-RAISED 2026-09-21: 'there's too many things here that get just dropped halfway through... not just more CI guards or whatever, not just building up the CLAUDE.md -- actually creating infra that has a pipeline that pulls things through to the finish.' THIS IS THE UNSOLVED PROBLEM THE RESET HAS SO FAR ONLY RELOCATED: archiving the registers removed where work rotted and did not build what pulls it through, so until this lands follow-through is WORSE than before -- the rows are in git history and nothing reads them. Design: plan section 3b. The pull is a scheduled render into the brief's section 0 plus a required same-day disposition, NOT a guard. The forcing function is that an unrouted due item appears on the OPERATOR'S page every day until routed, and the unrouted count is a number in section 5 -- which is the one structural difference from DUE.md, whose due-list was read by machinery that was read by nobody. Each of the five drop-reasons from plan 3b is asserted by a named self-test check with a negative control, so a later session cannot loosen one without turning a check red. [!] WHAT IS NOT DONE, AND IT IS THE HALF THAT MATTERS: nothing runs render_section_0 ON A SCHEDULE, because the brief that displays it is A3 and A3 is not built. A7 CANNOT BE CLOSED until section 0 renders on the operator's own page and the unrouted count appears as a number in section 5. Do not mark this done on the store alone. [!] The store is seeded EMPTY deliberately. Importing the 91 OPEN-ITEMS rows and 1,065 backlog rows is A8; dumping them in untriaged would fill section 0 with rows nobody dispositioned, which is the failure this replaces rather than a fast start. [!] A3a DISPATCHED 2026-09-21 (session_01AR9SV7kwUg8YBq38UVuVSN) as the lane that can close this. items.title: Rescue the 91 monitoring rows; triage the 1,065 archived backlog rows

No observation in 60 days and no named owner -> killed with terminal_reason 'unworked_since_<date>'. The 91 OPEN-ITEMS monitoring rows are the exception and come across whole. The blocked_on edge stated 'nowhere to import to until the pipeline exists' -- that condition is now satisfied, which is why this runs today rather than waiting on A3a. FRESH, sonnet-5. items.note: THE LOAD-BEARING CHANGE. Today check_dry_run_in_diff.py blocks turning a leg OFF and nothing blocks turning one ON; across 78 guards there is no counterpart. Demotion becomes free; promotion to a real-money roster requires a fresh evidence record clearing its declared bar. Tier-2 (CI + order-path policy) and needs the operator on the bar definition. Removing a leg from an account's strategies: roster is NOT guarded -- verified against the A6 diff, which removes two legs from alpaca_live and reports `clean`. SO B1 MUST KEY ON ROSTER MEMBERSHIP, not on the mode/execution fields: a guard watching only the fields can be walked around by editing the list, in either direction. This also matters for the mandates -- MD-PROMOTE-S1-S2 adds a leg to a roster, which is exactly the edit the current guard cannot see. [!] OPERATOR DECIDED THE BAR 2026-09-21: THE FOUR CLAUSES AS WRITTEN — named harness · stated n · net of the FULL cost stack · clearing a rule registered BEFORE the run. They were offered a fifth clause (an explicit minimum n, prompted by tlt_pullback_1d having reached a real-money roster on n=8) and declined it. RECORD THAT THEY WERE ASKED: the absence of a sample-size floor is now a decision, not an oversight, and a successor proposing one is re-opening a settled question rather than spotting a gap. [!] DISPATCHED 2026-09-21 on OPUS, not sonnet, and the reason is the task table's own rule rather than a preference: this guard decides what may reach a REAL-MONEY ROSTER. It writes no order, but it is the thing standing between a passing number and live capital once B5 removes the human, and 'anything on a real-money order path' is read here as including the gate on that path. [!] LANE FENCED HARD out of changing any roster, mode or execution VALUE — it builds the guard only. If the guard fails current main, that is a FINDING TO REPORT, not a licence to edit config. [!] TOLD the minimum-n clause was OFFERED AND DECLINED, so it does not re-add one and does not read its absence as a gap. [!] LANE RESULT 2026-09-21 -- PR #12688 (draft, landing=hold; the manager merges). scripts/ci/check_roster_promotion_evidence.py keys on ROSTER MEMBERSHIP (parsed roster at the fork point vs HEAD), registered in run_guards.py, 16 real-config tests, COVERAGE_FLOOR ratcheted 43->44. What is true and still a problem: that is a SUBSET assertion, deliberately, so it protects real money (no live leg without a paper counterpart) and does NOT make the mirror representative. Measured 2026-09-21: live 5 legs, mirror 14 -- nine mirror legs are not on the live book -- so Gate 2's demotion signal cannot be read off the mirror's aggregate. The test's own comment argues that asserting equality during a staged go-live would force alpaca_portfolio from 14 legs to 1 and destroy the paper research book. That argument is good and must be ANSWERED, not overwritten. [!] OPERATOR DECIDED 2026-09-21: STRICT EQUALITY, LIKE BYBIT. alpaca_portfolio carries exactly alpaca_live's roster, enforced by a test mirroring test_bybit_portfolio_mirrors_bybit_2_exactly. [!] THE COST WAS STATED WHEN ASKED AND IS ACCEPTED: the 9 surplus mirror legs stop accruing shadow ML data. Do not re-litigate that as a discovery. [!] DISPATCHED 2026-09-21 on OPUS: it edits config on accounts that trade, and although the mirror is paper, the roster it must match is alpaca_live's, which is real money. [!] LANE TOLD IT HAS NO OPERATOR OK FOR A TIER-2/3 CONFIG CHANGE. If the roster edit lands in those tiers it lands the Tier-1 half, states the exact one-line change, and STOPS — and it was told explicitly that leaving the new test RED against current config is a legitimate outcome that makes the gap loud, while weakening the test to go green is not. [!] AND TOLD NOT TO TOUCH alpaca_live: if the two differ, alpaca_live is the truth and the MIRROR moves. [!] POINTED at the `minus_proxies` carve-out in the existing test name, to establish whether it encodes real instruments that cannot mirror rather than deleting it silently — and at CLAUDE.md's record that an earlier session INFERRED 'no invariant exists' here and was wrong, so this is replacing a considered design with another, not fixing an oversight. (2) LADDER MANDATES — 'Grant all 5, S1->S2 gated': MD-PROMOTE-S0-S1, MD-PROMOTE-S1-S2, MD-DEMOTE-S2-S1, MD-DEMOTE-S1-OFF, MD-KILL-QUESTION all GRANTED; MD-PROMOTE-S1-S2 carries blocked_until = D3 shows realized cost within tolerance of modelled cost, enforced by the resolver, arming automatically when D3 passes. The bar and cap in this row's note (2026-09-21) stand. Deliverable order: (a) a small PR recording the ten grants verbatim in config/mandates.yaml (moves proposed->mandates; adds the five ladder entries with fires_when/never/evidence_required derived from this row and the manager skill); (b) the resolver + ping + section-1 render. B1 (the blocker) is done. OPERATOR GRANT 2026-09-21, verbatim: 'All the ladder decisions can be automated -- that is a standing mandate. Strategies can be promoted to live money without explicit operator approval if the evidence supports the decision. I should just get a ping in realtime of the update and an evidence review in the next daily briefing.' FIVE MANDATES ARE GRANTED: MD-PROMOTE-S0-S1, MD-PROMOTE-S1-S2 (REAL MONEY), MD-DEMOTE-S2-S1, MD-DEMOTE-S1-OFF, MD-KILL-QUESTION. [!] THE FILE IS NOT CREATED AHEAD OF THE RESOLVER -- a config nothing reads is the 'declared capability with no consumer' antipattern this repo already names. [!] WHAT CARRIES THE SAFETY IS 'if the evidence supports it': a COMMITTED evidence record, named harness, stated n, net of the FULL cost stack, clearing a rule registered before the run. A claim in a PR body is not a record; B1 is what makes that checkable. [!] MD-PROMOTE-S1-S2 MUST NOT ARM UNTIL D1 LANDS -- arithmetic, not caution: the harnesses default slippage and funding to 0.0, so every 'passed the backtest' verdict in today's corpus is fee-only and optimistic by an unknown amount (+0.57R on the one leg measured). items.title: Cost fidelity as the standing Gate-1 test
items.note:
Is realized slippage what the harness assumed, per leg? This is what makes the ladder traversable for SLOW legs: a 1d leg can never establish expectancy on paper in usable time (23 of 52 legs are unbounded_no_closes), but cost fidelity converges in a handful of trades because it measures a per-trade quantity. Divergence demotes the leg AND invalidates its Stage-0 record, because the backtest assumed a cost the venue does not charge. Same unit as D3. [!] UNBLOCKED 2026-09-21: E3 merged as 3afc02b, so the harnesses now price slippage and funding. The edge is discharged by the merge, not by waiting.
[2026-09-25 lane session_012kkcSiUFQ3asxUTqFybRHq, W4, dispatched by session_01Ljhs6sFAdWHdMDhJpL5aBP] RULE REGISTERED BEFORE THE RUN: RULE-R3-GATE1-COST-FIDELITY-v1 (docs/research/r3-gate1-cost-fidelity-rule-2026-09-25.md, commit 91a904e, pushed before any pull). Cell = (leg, account); D3's estimator (entry mean + package-referenced exit mean, 95% bootstrap CI); N_FLOOR 10 per side; T = MD-PROMOTE-S1-S2.bar.cost_tolerance_bps (0.0, read at run time, not a second number). divergent = CI lower > modelled+T -> demote one stage AND invalidate the Stage-0 record; consistent = CI upper <= modelled+T = the Gate-1 pass; else inconclusive; market cell beats simulator. MEASURED (pull 2026-09-25T13:23Z, comms/research/r3_cost_fidelity/2026-09-25.json, 55 legs / 83 cells): 0 divergent, 4 consistent (ict_scalp_5m on bybit_2 market; ict_scalp_avax_5m, ict_scalp_sol_5m, ict_scalp_xrp_5m on bybit_1 simulator -- ALL FOUR FAIL Stage 0, all four records over-charge), 0 inconclusive, 51 insufficient_n. Exit side binds: 162 package-referenced exits vs 1,257 entries. VENUES: only Bybit perps have n>=20 both sides -- market bybit_2 89/42, +1.14 bps CI [-0.75, +3.11] vs modelled 3.0 -> inconclusive (the 3.0 default, set as D3's CI upper 2.95, is now INSIDE the CI; two +11/+12 bps entries since D3). Alpaca: 0 measured exits on any account. IBKR: ib_paper 22/7 simulator, ib_live nothing. LANDED_UNPROVEN because 'standing' is not yet true: nothing re-runs it and nothing reads it. Closes when (1) the resolver's cost clause reads the R3 per-leg verdict instead of D3's venue point estimate (Tier-2 diff in the lane's final message, validated: tests/test_mandate_resolver.py 45 passed in a scratch worktree; needs matching fires_when text in config/mandates.yaml, the operator's) AND (2) a scheduled re-run (D3's weekly job) commits a dated record.

items.title: Retire what the reset orphaned
items.note: 67 guard scripts unreachable from run_guards.py, kept because 30+ live files still name their paths. Right call today, poor steady state. One bounded pass: delete with references, or record why it stays. NOT by bulk deletion -- the reference sweep IS the job. [!] SCOPE CORRECTED 2026-09-21: THE GUARD SCRIPTS WERE NOT THE ONLY ORPHAN, and the pattern is worth more than the list. The reset disarmed every workflow that WRITES to a retired register and swept none of the ones that READ one. A writer to a missing register fails loudly; a reader degrades to 'could not check' and keeps issuing advice about a file that is gone. Two were found the same day: (a) scope-overlap-audit.yml, which posted 'read the coordination board yourself' on the reset's own PR and is DISARMED in this pass; (b) scripts/ops/render_daily_brief.py + its test, five of whose six inputs were archived and whose guard (daily-brief-guard) was dropped in the same pass -- NOT deleted here, because A3 replaces it and removing a renderer before its replacement exists is how a capability goes missing quietly. [!] THE SWEEP THIS ROW OWES IS THEREFORE A READER SWEEP, not a deletion pass: for each path under docs/archive/2026-09-21-operating-reset/, find what still reads it. A grep for the archived FILENAMES across .github/ and scripts/ is the probe, and it needs a positive control -- the two above are it. [!] SCOPE WIDENED AGAIN 2026-09-21, and this one was found by the OPERATOR LOOKING AT THE PAGE rather than by my sweep -- which is the finding about the sweep. I scoped the reader hunt to .github/ and scripts/ and never looked at src/web/api/, so THE API THAT SERVES THE WORKFLOW PAGE still reads three archived registers and says so to the operator on every load: (a) a 'Live work sessions' panel reading docs/claude/work/SESSIONS.json, which degrades honestly to 'could not be read (absent)' but will never come back; (b) a WIP '0 / 8 in flight vs the declared ceiling' from the retired operating model; (c) THE WORK-STORE PANEL, which is the bad one -- src/web/api/routers/work.py:482-488 prints 'A bug to fix still goes to the review backlogs', instructing every reader to file into registers that are archived and unread. [!] THAT PANEL IS ACTIVE MISINFORMATION ON THE ONE PAGE BUILT TO PREVENT DROPPED WORK, so it outranks the rest of this row. It is a read path (Tier 1 per the tier table) but it is src/ and the route's tier must be checked against docs/api-tier-policy.md before editing. [!] THE LESSON FOR THE SWEEP ITSELF: 'grep the archived filenames' is the right probe but I ran it over the wrong POPULATION. The population is every consumer of an archived path ANYWHERE -- .github/, scripts/, src/, and the dashboard repo -- not the two directories I happened to be working in. [!] DISPATCHED 2026-09-21. MODEL UPGRADED haiku-4.5 -> sonnet-5, deliberately and against this row's own earlier value: this row's note records that the previous sweep ran over the WRONG POPULATION and that three of four orphan classes were found by something failing loudly or the operator looking at the page, not by the sweep. That is a judgement failure, not a throughput one, and haiku is the wrong instrument for it. The cheap-extraction half is instead being run SEPARATELY on the Fable pool as an independent cross-check (see E11) -- which gets the cheap model onto the cheap half without betting the sweep on it. [!] LANE TOLD the src/web/api/routers/work.py:482-488 panel OUTRANKS the 67 guard scripts, and that if budget runs short an honestly-bounded sweep REPORT beats a half-finished deletion pass. [!] THREE MORE INSTANCES FOUND ON 2026-09-21 WHILE THIS LANE WAS ALREADY RUNNING, all by running something rather than by a sweep, and they are FILED IN THE PIPELINE rather than added to this note so they cannot be lost if this lane lands without them: PI-20260921-0001 (trainer-VM serialization FIFO promised by two workflow comments, board archived -- routed to its own lane, session_01W7iGwkrozCQ8LYRSM8WgGE), PI-20260921-0002 (pr-landing-guard R13's first remedy message names the archived session-board.json, so every future Tier-1 self-landing PR is sent to a dead end before finding the working per-branch route), and PI-20260921-0003 (check_manager_scope.py derives WHO THE MANAGER IS from the archived MANAGER-LEASE.json, reports `no_manager_commits` on a branch with four manager commits, and EXITS 0 -- so the guard that enforces rule 1 of the manager contract fails OPEN while both CLAUDE.md and the manager SKILL still claim it is CI-enforced). [!] THE RUNNING TALLY IS NOW FIVE ORPHAN CLASSES AND FIVE FOUND THE HARD WAY. That is no longer an anecdote about one missed directory; it is evidence that a filename grep is the wrong PRIMARY probe. A guard or workflow that READS an archived register frequently does not name it in a greppable string at all -- it derives a path, or names it only in prose while the code reads a directory. The probe that actually caught 0002 and 0003 was RUNNING THE THING AND READING WHAT IT SAID. Consider adding that to this row's method: execute every guard in run_guards.py and every self-test, and treat `could not check`, `does not exist` and a green-on-nothing as findings. [!] CEILING BREACHED 2026-09-21: $22.73 against $20. Not killed -- the contract says read what the lane produced first, and the work is delivered in PR #12680. [!] BUT THE SWEEP IS INCOMPLETE and the Fable cross-check is how we know, which is exactly why E11 ran in parallel. That is simply wrong -- `landed_unproven` means MERGED with the effect not yet observed, and nothing here is merged. Set back to `in_flight`. Its PR (#12680) is MERGED, but the row was always going to outlive it -- E11's independent Fable probe reached four live reader surfaces this sweep did not, and PI-20260921-0001's lane flagged ~20+ non-archived files still live-reading board-pointer.json / session-board.json. items.title: armed-branch-push-watch races PR creation — every post-merge follow-up trips it
items.note: MEASURED 2026-09-21 on PR #12673, which is the follow-up to the reset's own merge. scripts/ci/check_armed_branch_push.py reported `dropped` (error, exit 1) on a HEALTHY push. Timing is the whole bug: #12668 squash-merged as 3ea2777 at 12:18 and GitHub deleted the branch; the branch was reset from the new main and A6 pushed at 12:25:43; #12673 was opened at 12:26:10. The watcher ran in that 27-second gap, when the branch's ONLY associated PR was the merged #12668 whose head.sha (1d596e2) is not the pushed sha (f3301d0). [!] THIS IS NOT A ONE-OFF. A PR cannot be opened for a branch that has not been pushed, so EVERY follow-up PR made the sanctioned way (git fetch origin main && git checkout -B <branch> origin/main) trips this between push and PR creation. The guard's premise -- that the PR it finds is the PR for this push -- is false during a branch reset. [!] DO NOT 'FIX' IT BY DOWNGRADING THE SEVERITY. The loss it exists for (#11846) is real, and a guard that cries wolf on the healthy path is how a guard gets ignored -- the desensitisation this repo already measured at 202 of 376 CRITICALs being one un-latched condition. Sharpen the condition. [!] THE DISCRIMINATOR, and it does NOT fall into the ancestry trap the script's own docstring warns about. That trap is asking whether a BRANCH commit reached main -- which a squash merge always answers no to. Ask the OPPOSITE: is the old PR's MERGE COMMIT an ancestor of the PUSHED commit? Branch correctly reset -> yes (3ea2777 is an ancestor of f3301d0), nothing lost, a new PR is coming. Genuine drop, i.e. more commits pushed onto the merged branch's old history -> no; the pre-merge head is the ancestor instead. A squash does not defeat that direction. [!] The script has an elaborate --self-test with a mutation-tested exact-sha comparison; extend it rather than loosening it, and add the branch-reset case as a NAMED fixture so the next person cannot re-introduce this by tightening something else. [!] DISPATCHED 2026-09-21, sonnet-5, fresh, ceiling $12 (this row carried no ceiling; one is set now). It earns its slot today because the manager's own pushes are the population it mis-grades: every follow-up PR made the sanctioned way trips it in the gap between push and PR creation. Lane told in terms to SHARPEN the condition and NOT downgrade the severity, and to CONSTRUCT both cases rather than implement the proposed discriminator on trust -- a reported hole beats a confident fix. [!] CLOSED 2026-09-21 AS ALREADY FIXED, AND THE LANE THAT ESTABLISHED IT WAS DISPATCHED IN ERROR BY THIS MANAGER. The fix landed in #12676 -- the SAME PR the handoff named as 'A7's pipeline + close-out contract + E10' -- and this row was never moved off `queued`. VERIFIED on main, not taken from the lane: scripts/ci/check_armed_branch_push.py defines RESET_FROM_MERGE, carries the merge-commit-ancestry discriminator, and has the branch-reset case as a named self-test fixture. Cost of the error: $0.93. [!] THE LESSON IS NOT 'READ MORE CAREFULLY', it is that a row's `state` was not moved by the PR that resolved it, so the register lied to the next reader in the direction of MORE work rather than less. Filed as PI-20260921-M06.

items.title: Employ the Fable weekly allowance — decide WHICH task classes, by measurement
items.note: OPERATOR DIRECTIVE 2026-09-21, verbatim: 'it should definitely be used when appropriate -- we want to employ that budget as well, we just want to make sure it is getting the tasks that are the best use of that resource.' So this row is NOT 'should we use it'. It is 'what goes there', and the answer must be measured rather than assumed. [!] WHY IT IS FREE CAPACITY: Settings > Usage shows Fable on a SEPARATE weekly limit from the main pool, measured 2026-09-21 at 0% used against a main pool at 68%. Work routed to Fable does not draw down the allowance the other lanes pace against, so this is additive headroom, not a trade-off between lanes. [!] THE SELECTION METHOD, because 'seems like a good fit' is how the wrong work lands on the wrong model. Pick the first class by ONE property: its output must be CHEAPLY VERIFIABLE against ground truth that already exists, so a bad fit is caught on the first run instead of propagating into a register. Run it on inputs a current-model lane has ALREADY done, diff the outputs, and widen only on that evidence. State the population of any quality claim, per RULE ONE. [!] WHAT THIS ROW MAY NOT DO, and it is the one hard edge: budget headroom is NEVER a reason to move work off the model its risk demands. .claude/skills/manager/SKILL.md already binds 'anything on a real-money order path' to opus. A cheaper pool does not relax that, and 'we had Fable budget spare' is not an argument that may ever appear next to an order-path change. [!] NOTHING IS MEASURED YET. No claim about Fable's fit for any lane in this repo has been made or tested as of 2026-09-21 -- the only established facts are that the pool exists, is separate, and is unused. Do not read a task list into this row that is not here. [!] FIRST FABLE ROUTING DECIDED AND DISPATCHED 2026-09-21, and the class chosen is GREP-AND-CLASSIFY SWEEP OVER A REPOSITORY. Chosen by this row's own stated method -- 'start with a class whose output is cheaply verifiable against work a current-model lane has already done, diff the two, and widen only on that evidence' -- so the probe runs IN PARALLEL with E9's sonnet sweep over the same needle set, and the diff is the measurement. [!] THE DUPLICATION IS THE DESIGN, not waste: Fable is a SEPARATE weekly allowance measured at 0% used, so this lane costs the main pool nothing and is additive capacity. [!] IT IS ALSO A REAL CROSS-CHECK regardless of what the diff shows, because this exact sweep has already been run once over the wrong population and missed src/web/api/ entirely. [!] SCOPED REPORT-ONLY -- one markdown file, no code changes, no fixes -- so a weak result costs a file nobody merges rather than a bad edit in src/. Given the three known positives as a mandatory probe control. [!] DO NOT read a good result here as authorising Fable on an order path: spare budget never moves work off the model its risk demands. [!] EARLY READ 2026-09-21, reported as an in-flight observation and NOT as the measurement: the Fable lane found all three mandated positive controls and was analysing a 2,090-line grep result while two of the five main-pool lanes were still stalled at zero work on an authenticity check. That is a signal about SPAWN HYGIENE (PI-20260921-0004), not about model quality, and must not be read as one -- the lanes that stalled had not started, so there is nothing to compare yet. The measurement is the DIFF against E9's sweep and it is not available until both land. [!] MEASURED AND DECIDED 2026-09-21. THE FABLE ROUTING IS VALIDATED FOR THIS CLASS and the evidence is not a vibe: the probe stated its population (282 archived basenames + 10 retired skill names + 6 work-store subdirs, over 8,540 tracked files, 2,931 hit lines in 1,197 files), found ALL THREE mandated positive controls including the one the previous sweep missed, gave its own methodology an honest caveat unprompted (`duty` is an English word, so set B was searched only in skill-reference shapes and a plain-prose mention is NOT in the report), and carried a 'what I could not determine' section. [!] IT ALSO OUT-FOUND THE SONNET LANE IT WAS RUN AGAINST, which is the diff E11 existed to produce: four live READER surfaces E9 did not reach, three of them user-facing -- the session-start hooks (PI-20260921-M05), docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md contradicting CLAUDE.md, the live-money runtime telling the operator to run an archived skill, and five CI guards reporting `clean` over an empty population. [!] CEILING BREACHED: $14.95 against $10. Read before judged, per the contract -- the overrun bought the population count and the classifier, which are the parts that make it checkable, so this is a ceiling set too low for the task rather than a lane that sprawled. Next sweep of this class gets $20. [!] WHAT THIS DOES NOT LICENSE: a good result on a bounded read-only sweep says nothing about an order path, and spare budget never moves work off the model its risk demands.

items.title: Tie a checklist row's state to the PR that resolved it
items.note: PROMOTED FROM PIPELINE ITEM PI-20260921-M06, 2026-09-21, because it is a BUILD and the taxonomy has exactly two categories: a question goes to research/queue/, a build gets a row here. Filing it only in the pipeline would have left it a memo. [!] ORIGIN: row E10 read `queued` while its fix was already merged in #12676, so the manager dispatched a lane against work that was done. $0.93, which is cheap; the MECHANISM is not. The register's state is hand-maintained by whoever remembers, and nothing ties a row to the PR that changed it. [!] THIS IS THE MIRROR OF THE FAILURE THE RESET EXISTS FOR: the reset's concern is work that silently STOPS, this is work that silently RESTARTS, and the same gap in the other direction is a row marked `done` that nobody did -- which is the expensive one. Live rows read mode `apply`, global_mode `apply`, apply_implemented true, apply_state `dispatchable` -- so MODE IS ALREADY ARMED and bybit_1 is evidently on the allowlist while breakout_1 is not. [!] THEREFORE THE CANDIDATE FIX IS AN ENV-VAR CHANGE ON THE LIVE VM (add breakout_1 to ARBITRATION_FANOUT_ACCOUNTS), NOT THE CODE CHANGE THIS ROW SCOPED. That is far narrower and far cheaper, and it is STILL TIER 3 -- it arms per-account binding on a FUNDED prop account, i.e. which account a real-money order routes to. Nothing here lands on this row's authority; the before/after election trace this row demands is now available from the soak. [!] ⚠️ DO NOT TREAT THIS AS CLEARANCE TO WIDEN. The standing caution from 2026-08-31 (ROADMAP S-PROBE-COVERAGE-EXPANSION) was that all 11 apply rows then on file read starved_count 0 on a single account, i.e. the path had only ever run where per-account election is a no-op. That is FALSE and is contradicted by the module docstring 60 lines above it ('apply IS IMPLEMENTED AS OF 2026-08-31') and by the live call site. It is an IMPOSSIBILITY CLAIM about an armable Tier-3 path -- the class docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md calls worse than a false success, because nobody re-checks a dead end. Tier-1 one-line fix; left out of this PR only to keep one PR to one concern. [!] OPERATOR DECISION 2026-09-22: ARM IT NOW, ON n=1. The question put to the operator was explicitly `arm on n=1` vs `gather more soak rows first`, with the n=1 stated (this is the first apply row ever read showing starved_count 1; all 11 prior rows read 0). They chose to arm. So this row is no longer blocked: the change is add breakout_1 to ARBITRATION_FANOUT_ACCOUNTS via the `set-env` system-action, PRESERVING bybit_1 rather than replacing it -- read the current value with `get-env` first (ARBITRATION_FANOUT_ACCOUNTS is already in get_env.py::ALLOWED_KEYS, checked), then write, then read back. [!] `landed_unproven` ON THE WRITE, NOT `done`: get-env reports `pending_restart` when the .env was edited and the service never re-read it, so the write alone proves nothing. CLOSING THIS ROW MEANS an arbitration_fanout_soak row showing apply_scope for breakout_1 as allowlisted AND its round in rounds_applied / rounds_written -- i.e. the elected leg actually binding, not merely being planned. [!] SUPERSEDED IN SCOPE 2026-09-22 by E33, on the operator's directive that arbitration be per-ACCOUNT generally rather than a one-account exception. items.note:

Work complete in two PRs, BOTH MERGE-PENDING with auto-merge armed: #12740 (the guard's identity + fail-closed + the planted 2026-09-21 regression) and #12742 (the three cost causes, the reconciler, the manager SKILL.md controls). `lane` is deliberately null rather than still naming the session: lane_reconcile.py's own `in_flight with NO lane` check now fires on this row, which is the correct alarm. MOVE THIS TO `landed_unproven` WHEN BOTH MERGE, and to `done` on the observation named at the end of this note. === WHAT WAS DELIVERED. (A) THE ROOT CAUSE, WHICH IS BIGGER THAN THE THREE COST LEAKS: scripts/ci/check_manager_scope.py derived manager identity only from MANAGER-LEASE.json, which the 2026-09-21 reset ARCHIVED, so the roster froze at 7 sessions (last run ending 2026-09-19T10:42:44Z) and could never grow. MEASURED over 635 commits: 12 dispatch acts, 1 session named, FALSE POSITIVES 0 of 1, the 6 self-lane-only sessions NOT admitted, FALSE NEGATIVES 7 of 7 vs the lease and STRUCTURAL (pre-reset `lane` held a team name: engineering 30, ops 29, research 18, zero session ids) which is why both sources stay. INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED by a surface I did not use: list_sessions' own `parent_session_id` names exactly 2 managers across 58 lanes — that day's (found by dispatch) and session_01GHpyXT2qssLJsrvXBQRkQF (found by the lease). The union covers both. (B) IT FAILS CLOSED, which matters more: no live identity source -> `no_identity_source`, live source with an empty roster -> `identity_unresolved`, BOTH FAIL at EXIT 2 (distinct from 1 for a real finding). It previously returned 7 stale ids and carried on. (C) THE REGRESSION IS PLANTED: --self-test 33 -> 40 cases. (D) THE TRAP WAS NOT WALKED INTO: 18 of the 38 still FAIL R2 after the change. Two paths were admitted, each the moved subject of an already-argued rule: .github/merge-slots/** graded PER COMMIT (own branch only), and research/queue/** as the surviving half of the 2026-09-03 operator ruling that filing is management. (E) THE THREE COST CAUSES, MEASURED LIVE 2026-09-22T13:02Z over the 60 most recent sessions, $5,892.69 readable of 51 of 60: 14 lanes over ceiling (B1 12.4x, not the six this row said — the row read running totals, its own cause 1); 22 finished-but-unarchived sessions holding $2,088.73; 4 BLOCKED lanes holding $1,347.60. [!] THE HEADLINE AND IT IS 30x THIS ROW'S ESTIMATE: session_01XYu2vvg9Qgxoqf4jJQyd8i (ENGINEERING LANE MI-305, spawned by the PREVIOUS manager 2026-09-18) has sat BLOCKED and IDLE 72.8 hours holding $1,343.06 and has NEVER COMMITTED A LINE — more than this row's entire 13-lane day in one session that produced nothing. Filed as PI-20260922-ONE-BLOCKED-LANE-HAS-HELD-1343-USD-FOR-72-HOURS-HAVING-NEVER-COMMITTED-A-LINE-AND-22-FINISHED-LANES-SIT-UNARCHIVED. A walled lane needs a HUMAN to clear its prompt and archiving another manager's lanes is the MANAGER's call, so it is surfaced, not cleared. (F) THE INVOLUNTARY MECHANISM IS BUILT, TRIED AND HONESTLY NOT WORKING. Two cheaper designs were KILLED ON MEASUREMENT first: a CI guard on git commit recency (5 of 7 WORKING lanes had NEVER committed, so it would have redded five healthy lanes) and a CI guard on the offline half (it would fail contributors for the manager's behaviour). The chosen design — a Routine firing a FRESH session, so the manager is not in the path — was created, FIRED ONCE, and DISABLED the same minute: the fired session has no repo checkout and no MCP connectors, so it can neither run the script nor call list_sessions. THE INVARIANT IS THEREFORE STILL VOLUNTARY and says so; what stands is a DISCIPLINE in SKILL.md, labelled as one. Filed as PI-20260922-THE-LANE-WATCHDOG-ROUTINE-FIRES-SESSIONS-WITH-NO-REPO-AND-NO-MCP-SO-IT-IS-DISABLED-AND-THE-INVARIANT-IS-STILL-VOLUNTARY — the operator must attach the connector + source in the Routines UI, which a session cannot do. (G) ALSO FILED, found while fixing R2 and not walked past: R6/R7/R8's subjects are ALL absent on main too, so three of four rules grade nothing and two did it silently — PI-20260922-MANAGER-SCOPE-R6-R7-R8-HAVE-NO-SUBJECT-AFTER-THE-RESET-SO-THREE-OF-FOUR-RULES-GRADE-NOTHING. === REACHED: MERGED is not yet true (both PRs armed, not merged). DEPLOYED and OBSERVED are not claimed for anything in this row. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: check_manager_scope.py printing `identity source `dispatch`: live` with the current manager on the roster, AND a `violation` on a real PR graded from main rather than from a branch. === WHAT THIS ROW'S ORIGINAL TEXT GOT WRONG, kept so it is not re-quoted: 'six lanes exceeded theirs' is 14 when measured after archiving, and 'final spends read off get_session' is only true via external_metadata.usage.cost_usd, which is ABSENT on 9 of 60 sessions — 6 of them WORKING — so an unreadable cost must render as could-not-look, never $0. === ORIGINAL ROW TEXT FOLLOWS === MEASURED 2026-09-21 across 12 dispatched lanes, final spends read off get_session: roughly $860 against ceilings totalling ~$250. Six lanes exceeded theirs; two exceeded by more than 6x (B1 $270.39/$35, B2 $229.13/$30). [!] THREE DISTINCT CAUSES, and they need different fixes -- lumping them as 'lanes are expensive' would fix none. (1) A CEILING NOBODY CHECKS MID-FLIGHT IS NOT A CEILING. Nothing reads spend during a run; the manager set ceilings and looked once, at the end. A1's meter now exists and this is its first real consumer. (2) FINISHED LANES KEEP SPENDING. A9 went $37.13 -> $50.78 AFTER its work merged, sitting subscribed to its own PR; E16 went $25.38 -> $56.14 the same way. Watching a PR is not free and the lane has nothing left to contribute to it. Archive on merge, or do not subscribe a lane to the PR the manager is going to merge anyway. (3) AN UNATTENDED LANE CAN HIT AN INTERACTIVE PERMISSION PROMPT AND SPEND ITS WHOLE BUDGET THERE. B2 did, twice. The second attempt's pending action was readable and specific: a COMPOUND, PIPED git command (`git fetch ... 2>&1 | tail -5 && git merge ... 2>&1 | tail -60`) awaiting a Bash approval nobody was present to give. ⚠️ THAT COMMAND SHAPE IS A HYPOTHESIS, NOT ESTABLISHED -- other lanes committed and pushed all day, so it is not universal. Establish WHICH shapes are refused before writing a rule about it; a dispatch instruction based on a guess would be the same category of error this repo keeps paying for. [!] THE CHEAPEST FIX IS PROBABLY (2) AND IT IS FREE: stop subscribing lanes to PRs the manager merges. [!] ⚠️ THE TOTAL ON THIS ROW WAS WRONG WHEN IT WAS WRITTEN, AND THE ERROR WAS THIS ROW'S OWN CAUSE (1). It said ~$860. Read again after every lane was ARCHIVED, the total is ~$1,142 across 13 lanes. B1 alone is $435.05, not the $270.39 committed a few hours earlier -- it accrued $165 MORE while IDLE, watching the PR the manager was about to merge anyway. A1 is $59.17, not $28.03. [!] SO THE MANAGER MADE THE SAME MISTAKE TWICE IN ONE DAY, the second time inside the commit describing the mistake. The mechanism is exact and unglamorous: get_session on a LIVE lane returns a RUNNING total, and a running total written onto a row reads like a final one. [!] THE RULE IS MECHANICAL, NOT 'be more careful': A LANE'S SPEND IS FINAL ONLY ONCE THE LANE IS ARCHIVED. Read it there, or record it with the read-time and the word `running` beside it. A number with no read-time is the same defect as a count that cannot say whether anyone looked. [!] AND IT SHARPENS CAUSE (2) from 'lanes keep spending' into a SIZE: the idle-watching tail is the single largest line in the day's spend, larger than any lane's actual work. [!] AND ONE MORE INSTANCE, CAUGHT IN THE ACT WHILE WRITING THIS ROW: resolving the checklist conflict with a 'longest note wins' heuristic silently reverted B1's state from `done` to `in_flight`. A heuristic that cannot say WHY it chose a side is the same defect as a count that cannot say whether anyone looked. States are now set explicitly from the merges performed, and the heuristic is not reused.  === E20 LANE UPDATE 2026-09-22 (session_011xpvJ2MQgd4jmKkdfg6gzV, branch claude/e20-manager-identity-fail-closed). THE ROOT CAUSE IS BIGGER THAN THE THREE COST LEAKS AND IS FIXED FIRST. Mechanism: scripts/ci/check_guard_liveness.py, WIRED into run_guards.py, report-first with a shrink-only baseline so it does not red-wall the repo on day one. [!] AND THE STRUCTURAL HALF, built after the manager supplied the design constraint that FRESHNESS BELONGS IN CI RATHER THAN ON A TIMER — because the obvious fix (emit receipts, grade their freshness) IS check_manager_queue_watch, i.e. instance #3, so a scheduled grader can always be the thing that did not fire while CI's own liveness is proven by PRs merging at all. scripts/ci/check_cadence_liveness.py, WIRED as `cadence-liveness`, DERIVES its population from the tree (workflow `schedule:` crons + deploy/*.timer OnCalendar) and FAILS on anything derived-but-unregistered, so omission is detectable rather than a hand-maintained list. The 37 split into 8 that already commit back (one declared output path from gradeable, the cheap shrink) and 29 with no in-repo trace at all. [!] RESIDUAL NAMED IN A DISCLOSURE PRINTED ON EVERY RUN: a ROUTINE is not derivable from the repo, so a Routine's omission is NOT detected — and instance #3 was a Routine. Both halves of this class bottom out in the SAME operator action: attach the connector and a source to the Routines, or delete them. [!] OBSERVED 2026-09-22T14:35Z, AND THIS IS THE THING THE ROW HANGS ON — not the merge. #12740 merged as 76a58117; the guard was then run FROM MAIN against a real branch (the first attempt ran the BRANCH's copy, which predated the merge and printed the old output — recorded because it is the same 'wrong version' error the row is about). items.title: The exit monitor's registry-failure fallback covers 0 of 52 routed-live legs
items.note: MEASURED 2026-09-22 by parsing config/strategies.yaml (55 declared) + config/accounts.yaml (11 accounts) at 0d3ab95: 52 distinct strategies are routed to at least one `mode: live` account. src/runtime/pipeline.py:349-351 returns the hardcoded fallback ['turtle_soup','vwap'] whenever load_strategies() raises. NEITHER name is routed to any live account -- turtle_soup is `execution: shadow`, vwap is `enabled: false` + `execution: shadow`. The set difference is 52 of 52. [!] THIS IS NOT ONLY AN ENTRY-SIDE LIST. `STRATEGIES` is what the EXIT half iterates: run_exit_evaluation_tick calls _load_strategies(None) -> pipeline.STRATEGIES, then get_order_packages_by_strategy per name. On the fallback, every open package belonging to the other 52 legs receives NO monitor() call -- no trailing amend, no stale-exit, no giveback stop, no exit head. Open REAL-MONEY positions would sit unmanaged until a broker-side bracket or the reconciler caught them. [!] THE TRIGGER IS REACHABLE. STRATEGIES is a module-level constant evaluated once at import and the fallback fires on ANY load_strategies() exception -- a malformed config/strategies.yaml being the live one. ict-git-sync pulls main every ~5 min, so a YAML syntax error landing on main reaches the live trader inside ~5 minutes. [!] AND IT IS SILENT. One logger.warning at import. None of the health snapshot's 7 checks (service, git_drift, git_fetch, tick, accounts_api, db, disk) would go red -- the process is alive, ticking, in sync, and the DB answers. The snapshot keeps reading `7/7 checks ok`. [!] FIELD BEATS COMMENT: the comment at pipeline.py:350 asserts the fallback `matches the production roster in config/strategies.yaml after PR B1`. Measured today it matches 0 of 52 -- the same shape as the trainer flock comment fixed in de20550. [!] SECOND, SEPARATE COLLAPSE at order_monitor.py:124-126: _load_strategies returns [] on exception, and the tick then returns {} summaries -- `we could not resolve the strategy list` and `no strategy had anything open` are indistinguishable downstream. [!] PROPOSED FIX, not applied (Tier-2, and /health-review may not touch src/): (1) delete the VALUE fallback -- on registry failure raise, or return a sentinel callers must branch on; a trader that cannot read its own roster must not silently run a two-name one. (2) Make the exit half's population open-package-driven (SELECT DISTINCT strategy FROM order_packages WHERE status='open') UNION the roster, so an open position is monitored because it IS OPEN, never because it appears in a list. (3) Add a health check comparing len(STRATEGIES) against the enabled count in strategies.yaml. [!] REFUTED HYPOTHESIS, recorded so it is not re-derived: the TLT position open on alpaca_live (id 5924, pattern tlt_pullback_1h, opened 2026-09-18) belongs to a leg A6/#12673 pulled from the alpaca_live ROSTER on 2026-09-21, and is NOT stranded -- exit evaluation iterates the strategies.yaml registry, not account rosters, and tlt_pullback_1h is still enabled there (r-block updated 05:29Z). Roster removal does not strand an open position; registry FAILURE would strand all of them. [!] LANE session_014LSHstYGrXDTZnNW5kgjn8, 2026-09-22, branch `e21-exit-monitor-roster-resolution`. RE-MEASURED INDEPENDENTLY rather than inherited, by parsing config/strategies.yaml (55 declared) + config/accounts.yaml (11 accounts) at f3746ab: 52 distinct strategies routed to >=1 `mode: live` account; the fallback covered 0 of 52; turtle_soup `execution: shadow`, vwap `enabled: false` + `execution: shadow`. The review's numbers hold. That re-measurement is now a TEST (tests/test_e21_exit_roster_resolution.py::test_the_retired_fallback_covered_no_live_leg), so the comment cannot drift from the config again. [!] DECIDED (this lane, arguing the question the dispatch posed): THE ENTRY AND EXIT SIDES GET DIFFERENT ANSWERS, because the question 'fall back to a list, or refuse' is only hard while the exit half depends on that list. (1) ENTRY: no value fallback at all. `resolve_roster()` returns a three-state resolution (ok/empty/unreadable) and `STRATEGIES` is EMPTY on `unreadable`, so the trader opens nothing rather than opening the wrong two names. This is NOT the trader switching itself off (Prime Directive rule 2): no account `mode:` is written, no breaker latches, the process keeps ticking and comes up live on the next boot per YAML; it is a per-condition refusal with a logged cause, the same shape as `pipeline.strategy_builders()`, which is deliberately un-wrapped on the stated ground that 'a rollback that cannot resolve its roster must fail loudly rather than resolve to an empty dict and silently trade nothing'. And the old fallback was ALREADY a near-total entry halt -- 0 of 52 -- only a silent one that additionally re-enabled two deliberately non-executing legs. (2) EXIT: does not consult the roster state to decide what to monitor AT ALL. `order_monitor.exit_population()` is `SELECT DISTINCT strategy_name FROM order_packages WHERE status='open'` UNION the roster, in roster order. A position is monitored because it is OPEN. That is what makes (1) safe: refusing to open new positions no longer costs exit management of the open ones. [!] REQUIREMENT 3 (positions whose leg left the roster) IS ADDRESSED, AND THE ROW'S OWN REFUTED HYPOTHESIS IS CONFIRMED CORRECT rather than re-derived: exit evaluation never read ACCOUNT rosters, so A6/#12673 removing tlt_pullback_1h from alpaca_live's roster did not strand the open TLT position -- VERIFIED this session by reading src/strategy_registry.py::load_strategies, which does not filter on `enabled` or `execution` and returns all 55 declared names, and run_exit_evaluation_tick, which iterates that list. THE RESIDUAL GAP IS REGISTRY REMOVAL, NOT ROSTER REMOVAL: a leg deleted from strategies.yaml (or the whole file becoming unreadable) while holding an open position WAS stranded, and row R2 cuts four more legs. The union closes that, and is pinned end-to-end by test_exit_tick_scans_an_open_package_off_the_roster, which drives a real sqlite journal through run_exit_evaluation_tick. [!] REQUIREMENT 2 (not silent): new health check `strategy_roster` in src/runtime/health.py, added to _DEFAULT_CHECKS so the snapshot carries 8 rather than 7. `unreadable` and `empty` are BOTH critical and carry DIFFERENT ctx.state + detail -- the collapsed-state standard is that they must not render identically, not that they must grade differently. Registered as contract `strategy_roster.roster_state` in scripts/ci/check_collapsed_states.py; the guard reports `3 consumer(s), all states read`. The check re-reads the YAML through `strategy_registry.reload_strategies()` because the registry caches after first load -- without that bypass the check would answer from the last good read forever and could never fire, which is pinned by test_health_check_rereads_the_file_rather_than_a_cached_roster. [!] PROOF THE TESTS ARE A REGRESSION TEST AND NOT DECORATION: 11 tests, all passing on the branch. Re-run with src/ restored to f3746ab (the new module src/runtime/strategy_roster.py necessarily stays, since `git checkout <rev> -- src/` cannot remove a file that did not exist at that rev): 9 of 11 FAIL. Against a pristine f3746ab worktree the module errors at collection, i.e. 11 of 11. The 2 that pass in the hybrid run are the two config re-measurements, which are true of both revisions by construction. [!] STATUS, and the three words kept apart: MERGED - no (draft PR, held for the manager per the lane's dispatch). DEPLOYED - no. OBSERVED - no, and it CANNOT be yet: `STRATEGIES` is module-level and evaluated once at import, so nothing here reaches the live trader until ict-trader-live RESTARTS after the deploy; ict-git-sync pulls main every ~5 min. Filed as PI-20260922-NW5KGJN8-0001 with the two separate observations that would close it (a `strategy_roster` row in a vm-diag snapshot for the web-api half; a trader journalctl restart or the E21 off-roster warning for the exit half). This row must not go past `landed_unproven` on the merge alone. [!] CORRECTION, same session, before anyone acts on this row: an earlier draft of this note and of PR #12710 said ict-git-sync 'does not restart the trader'. That is WRONG and is withdrawn. VERIFIED by reading deploy/ict-git-sync.service (ExecStart=bash scripts/deploy_pull_restart.sh) and scripts/deploy_pull_restart.sh: the deploy DOES `systemctl restart ict-trader-live ict-telegram-bot ict-web-api`, gated on runtime_logs/deployed_sha.txt rather than on whether this fetch moved HEAD, and skips the restart only for a diff whose every path is non-runtime (docs/, tests/, .claude/, .github/, top-level *.md). This diff touches src/, so the restart fires and `deployed` follows `merged` within about one 5-minute tick. `observed` is still separate and still needs the two reads in PI-20260922-NW5KGJN8-0001. [!] MERGED 2026-09-22: PR #12710 squash-merged to main (the PR head 7d00831b0 is NOT an ancestor of main -- squash -- so verify by CONTENT, not by sha). VERIFIED on origin/main: src/runtime/strategy_roster.py present; `return ["turtle_soup", "vwap"]` occurs 0 times in src/runtime/pipeline.py; `def exit_population` present in src/runtime/order_monitor.py. STATE IS `landed_unproven`, NOT `done`, and the distinction is load-bearing: STRATEGIES is a module-level constant evaluated once at import, so the fix takes effect only when ict-trader-live restarts -- automatic within ~one 5-min git-sync tick, but a restart having been ISSUED is not the check appearing in a snapshot. THE OBSERVATION THAT CLOSES THIS ROW is PI-20260922-NW5KGJN8-0001's clears_when: a vm-diag snapshot carrying a `strategy_roster` health check with ctx.state=='ok' and ctx.resolved==ctx.declared (a snapshot showing 7 checks and no strategy_roster means the deploy has NOT landed), plus a trader journalctl restart later than the deploy commit for the exit half. [!] CI RESULT, recorded because it answers the one bullet this lane could not: on the merged head, `pytest-run`, `pytest-collect`, `Guards` and `repo-inventory` all PASSED. `merge-claim-audit` FAILED, and it is not this change's -- it checks out main and dies on an archived board-pointer.json, filed as PI-20260922-NW5KGJN8-0002. [!] THIS LANE GOT CI WRONG TWICE BEFORE FINDING THAT: it read `get_status`, which returns only legacy commit statuses (total_count 0) and cannot see Actions check runs, and reported 'no red CI'. A zero from a probe that cannot see the thing is not a zero.ANAGER 2026-09-22: MERGED as 9eb13192. NOT deployed, NOT observed -- which is why this is `landed_unproven` and not `done`. CLOSING THIS ROW MEANS observing a live tick calling monitor() on an open order package whose strategy_name is NOT in the roster. The standing worked example is already open: the real-money TLT position, pattern tlt_pullback_1h, opened 2026-09-18, on a leg A6 removed from alpaca_live's roster on 2026-09-21.

items.title: The health snapshot reports 7/7 ok while structurally unable to see the failure that happened
items.note: MEASURED 2026-09-22T05:30Z from /api/bot/health/latest (snapshot ts 05:16:31Z): status ok, summary `7/7 checks ok`, action_required false. The seven checks are service, git_drift, git_fetch, tick, accounts_api, db, disk. The accounts_api check's OWN detail string reads: `all 8 recorded broker-API accounts ok (1 manual-bridge skipped: breakout_1; 2 dry/shelved skipped: ib_live, oanda_practice)`. [!] breakout_1 IS THE FUNDED PROP ACCOUNT THAT RECEIVED ZERO TICKETS FOR THREE WEEKS (row E16, measured 21 of 21). The account check EXCLUDES it by construction -- it is the one account skipped -- and no check among the seven asks whether signals, intents or tickets are still being PRODUCED. The surface the operator looks at was green throughout the failure and would be green through the next one. [!] CROSS-CHECKED against /api/bot/accounts/balances: breakout_1 balance null, open_positions null, api_ok false. The DATA is honest (null, not 0 -- the repo's own render rule followed correctly). The defect is that nothing GRADES it: an account permanently api_ok:false is indistinguishable from one that just went dark. [!] COMPLEMENTS E18, does not duplicate it. E18 builds the missing detector (intents produced vs tickets received). This row is narrower and cheaper: the EXISTING all-clear counts a structurally-skipped account toward 7/7. [!] PROPOSED FIX (Tier-1, reporting only, no runtime path): (a) report skipped accounts as a distinct state in the summary line -- `7/7 ok, 3 accounts NOT CHECKED` rather than folding them into ok; (b) add a per-routed-account last-ticket-age check, which is the check whose absence E16 measured. [!] E18 BOUNDARY, ARGUED ON THE ROW AS ASKED -- AND THE ANSWER IS THAT E22 IS **BOTH** HALVES SPLIT, NOT ONE CHOICE. The row proposed two fixes and they belong to different owners. (a) 'report skipped accounts as a distinct state' IS E22's OWN and has nothing to do with E18: it is a collapsed state in the REPORTING arithmetic -- `7/7 checks ok` counted an exclusion as a pass -- and it is wrong independently of whether any detector ever exists. BUILT HERE. (b) 'add a per-routed-account last-ticket-age check' IS E18's SIGNAL and is NOT built here: putting it in the snapshot writer would be exactly the second, drifting implementation this row was told not to become. When E18 lands it reports its own verdict; the snapshot keeps saying only what was and was not EXAMINED. [!] SO THE TWO ROWS COMPOSE RATHER THAN OVERLAP: E18 answers 'is that account still being FED?' (a detector that must exist and does not). E22 answers 'does the all-clear admit it did not LOOK?' (an arithmetic bug in a surface that already exists). Neither substitutes. [!] BUILT, Tier-2, reporting-only: scripts/write_health_snapshot.py::build_payload now emits a top-level `not_checked: {accounts[], count, by_check{}}` and appends `; N account(s) NOT CHECKED: <names>` to the summary line. Keyed on each check's own `ctx` lists (skipped / shelved / no_data), NEVER parsed out of the `detail` prose -- the prose is a claim about the check, the ctx is the check's record of what it did. The accounts_api check already emitted all three, so no producer change was needed. [!] `no_data` IS INCLUDED DELIBERATELY AND IS THE DANGEROUS MEMBER, which the row did not name: the accounts_api check subtracts it from its OWN headline (`all {total - len(no_data)} ... ok`), so a declared-live account WITH a broker API whose reading never arrived passes exactly as quietly as a manual bridge that was never eligible. That is 'we could not look' wearing 'ok', the same collapse one level down. [!] ⚠️ WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE, AND WHY, so a later change does not make it quietly: `status` and `action_required` ARE UNMOVED. A manual bridge is skipped on EVERY snapshot for its whole life, so grading the exclusion `watch` would put one permanent condition on every snapshot forever -- the desensitised alarm the canonical rules already call a P1 (BL-20260823-TARGET-NAKED-COOLDOWN put ONE condition on 53.7% of the operator's ERROR+ feed by that exact mechanism), and the same refusal soak_alarm's `accruing` state makes. A permanent amber is not a detector. There is a test asserting the refusal so it cannot be reversed silently. THE ROW'S BAR IS STILL MET: `7/7 ok` is no longer SAYABLE alone -- the summary string itself now carries the named excluded accounts, and the summary is the field /api/bot/health/latest serves and that E22 measured. [!] VALIDATION: 82 tests pass locally (tests/test_write_health_snapshot.py 14, incl. 5 new, plus test_health.py and test_exit_loop_health.py). The five new ones assert the exact 2026-09-22 snapshot shape (7/7 with breakout_1 + ib_live + oanda_practice NAMED, not merely counted), the `no_data` case, the dedup/union across checks, the unmoved status, and a POSITIVE CONTROL FOR THE NEGATIVE -- `count: 0` with the field PRESENT is a real measurement ('every account was examined') and is distinguishable from a check that emitted no ctx at all, which is visible by its absence from `by_check`. ⚠️ NOT run locally: the router test (tests/test_diag_exit_loop_health_reachable.py) -- fastapi is not installed in this sandbox, so that one is CI's to run; said rather than claimed. [!] STATE: NOT `done` and not observable from here. This writer runs ON the live VM under ict-health-snapshot.timer, so merged != deployed != observed. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a /api/bot/health/latest read whose `summary` carries `account(s) NOT CHECKED` and whose `not_checked.accounts` names breakout_1 -- one diag pull after the next deploy. [!] MANAGER 2026-09-22: MERGED as b6e87b2b. NOT deployed, NOT observed. CLOSING THIS ROW MEANS reading /api/bot/health/latest and seeing breakout_1 reported as a GRADED skip instead of folded into `7/7 checks ok` -- i.e. the summary distinguishing `we did not look` from `we looked and found nothing` for that account.

items.title: The health-review skill's hard completion gate points at a file the reset archived
items.note: MEASURED 2026-09-22: .claude/skills/health-review/SKILL.md names docs/claude/health-review-backlog.json in five places, including the section headed `Draining the backlog -- a HARD COMPLETION GATE (not a sample)` and the Output contract's `backlog_coverage.count_untriaged` MUST be 0. `ls docs/claude/health-review-backlog.json` -> No such file or directory; it was archived by the 2026-09-21 reset. [!] SO THE GATE IS UNSATISFIABLE AND EVERY HEALTH-REVIEW FROM THE RESET ONWARD IS EITHER INCOMPLETE BY ITS OWN CONTRACT OR QUIETLY IGNORING IT. The same file is also the skill's WINDOW anchor (`the newest backlog_drain timestamp`), so the review window has no anchor either -- this review had to open its window at the reset and say so. A binding skill at instruction-hierarchy level 5 instructing something that cannot be done is the defect class the canonical rules already record at `THIS RULE NAMED FIVE OTHER WORDS UNTIL 2026-09-12 AND NOT ONE OF THEM WAS A LEGAL status`. [!] AND THE OUTPUT TEMPLATE HAS THE SAME SHAPE OF GAP: comms/schema/health_review_response.template.json's findings status enum is `ok | watch | concern`, with NO value for `we did not look`. Under a diag outage the template FORCES an unmeasurable dimension to be rendered as a measurement outcome -- exactly the collapse docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md 'Collapsed states' forbids and scripts/ci/check_collapsed_states.py enforces elsewhere. This review emitted `could_not_look` and declared the deviation rather than comply. [!] PROPOSED FIX (Tier-1): re-point the skill's backlog sections at docs/claude/work/PIPELINE.jsonl + MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json, re-anchor the window on the newest file under comms/reviews/health/, and add `could_not_look` to the template enum -- registering the three-way contract in collapsed-state-guard's CONTRACTS table is the mechanical form. [!] FIXED 2026-09-22 BY THIS LANE, and the GATE IS KEPT RATHER THAN REMOVED -- a review that leaves open items unlooked-at has still not done its job, and that reasoning did not expire with the file. What changed is only WHERE the open set lives. [!] THE BREAK IS WIDER THAN THE ROW SUSPECTED AND IT IS MEASURED, not inferred. `ls docs/claude/*-review-backlog.json` 2026-09-22: ALL FOUR are absent -- health-review-backlog.json, performance-review-backlog.json, research-review-backlog.json, ml-review-backlog.json. So this is not a health-review problem found first; it is ONE break with FOUR instances. /performance-review and /ml-review carry the IDENTICAL 'HARD COMPLETION GATE (not a sample)' heading and the IDENTICAL backlog_coverage.count_untriaged == 0 output contract over files that are not there. THEIR GATES ARE STILL BROKEN and are NOT fixed here -- recorded deliberately, because each is its own skill with its own output template and its own owned surfaces, and repointing all three would be one PR to three concerns. The fix for each is mechanically the same edit; a new table in the health-review skill names them so a session running either sibling meets the fact instead of re-deriving it. [!] WHAT LANDED, in .claude/skills/health-review/SKILL.md (7 stale refs -> 2, and both survivors are deliberate historical citations that SAY the file is gone): (1) THE WINDOW ANCHOR now reads the newest file under comms/reviews/health/ -- the directory this skill's own output lands in, so it is written by this review and by nothing else, with a fallback to the channel ping and then 24h. ⚠️ Recorded beside it: `git log` of the ARCHIVE is history, not an anchor -- it stopped moving when the file was archived, so it would pin the window open forever. That is the trap a later session would otherwise reach for. (2) THE GATE now computes its open set as a COUNTED UNION of two live surfaces: PIPELINE.jsonl (`python3 scripts/ops/pipeline.py --due`, because DUE IS COMPUTED and must not be hand-picked) and the MANAGER-CHECKLIST rows this review OWNS. Write-back routes each item to the surface it came from, with pipeline closes needing a terminal_reason and `killed` named as a first-class outcome. (3) THE OUTPUT CONTRACT now requires backlog_coverage to NAME ITS SOURCES and per-surface counts. `open_at_start: 0` over an unstated population is the same collapsed state one level up -- 'there was nothing open' and 'I could not read the open set' are opposite findings -- and an unreadable surface reports could_not_look WITHOUT shrinking the denominator. (4) The frontmatter description, the step-13 checklist line, and the three FILING destinations (compliance-audit drift, artifact-validity findings, orphan-trade findings) now point at PIPELINE.jsonl VIA scripts/ops/pipeline.py, with 'never by hand' stated -- the script enforces due_when + origin.rerun + an explicit intent=, and the file is append-only JSONL, never a JSON array. [!] ⚠️ THE ARCHIVED BACKLOG IS NOT RESURRECTED and the skill now says so in terms, with the second half the row did not state: the 1,065 archived rows are ALSO NOT IMPORTED (that is A8, and most should be KILLED explicitly rather than carried), so the new denominator is the LIVE open set and not the historical one -- and saying which is part of satisfying the gate. [!] AND THE TEMPLATE HALF IS DONE: comms/schema/health_review_response.template.json now reads `ok | watch | concern | could_not_look` on all 17 findings dimensions, with a _comment_status_enum recording WHY -- the old enum had no value for a dimension that could not be MEASURED, so under a diag outage it FORCED an unmeasurable dimension to render as a measurement outcome. It bit on 2026-09-22 on the mandatory security dimension (0 of 5 sources swept), where the honest answer was none of the three. The comment states that could_not_look is NEVER an all-clear, must name which source was unreachable and why, and is NOT a substitute for `watch` (an unconfirmed signal we DID see). [!] ⚠️ NOT DONE, stated rather than implied: registering the three-way contract in scripts/ci/check_collapsed_states.py's CONTRACTS table -- the MECHANICAL form this row's own proposed fix names. The enum is now WRITABLE but nothing FAILS a review that never emits could_not_look, and per the canonical rules a state nothing branches on is already collapsed. That is the residue and it is the next unit of work on this row. [!] MANAGER 2026-09-22: MERGED as d6c9ea74 and `done` rather than `landed_unproven` because the effect IS the merged text -- a skill read at instruction-hierarchy level 5 takes effect on the next read, with no deploy between merge and effect. Verified by reading the merged file, not inferred from the PR body.

items.title: The mandatory security stated-negative could not be produced, and was not faked
items.note: The health-review skill is explicit that a clean breach check must be a STATED VERIFICATION and that an empty security finding is a review failure.
