items.title: Two workflows fail on EVERY push to main, both because the reset archived a register nothing swept the readers of
items.note: MEASURED 2026-09-22 by me while landing the merge wave. POPULATION: the 100 most recent COMPLETED workflow runs on `main`, window 06:38:10Z -> 07:53:57Z (every push of this session's merge wave), across 53 distinct workflows. RESULT: 2 of 53 fail, and BOTH fail 6 of 6 with ZERO successes -- `reconcile-open-prs` and `work-digest`. [!] A THIRD, `merge-claim-audit`, fails on PR heads rather than on main, OBSERVED on 8867208 at 07:52Z. [!] ROOT CAUSES READ FROM THE LOGS, NOT INFERRED. merge-claim-audit: `scripts/ci/board_pointer.py --self-test` prints `could_not_check -- docs/claude/board-pointer.json does not exist -- the board cannot be resolved` and exits 1; that file was deleted by 3ea2777, the 2026-09-21 operating reset that retired the coordination board. reconcile-open-prs: `scripts/ops/reconcile_open_prs.py:269` raises `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get'` because the loader returns None for the archived docs/claude/work/OPEN-PRS.json -- IT DOES NOT EVEN SAY THE FILE IS GONE, it dies on a NoneType, which is the collapsed-state failure one level up: `we could not look` rendered as a crash rather than as a state. work-digest's cause is NOT established -- I did not read its log, and this row must not be read as claiming I did. [!] THIS IS THE SAME DEFECT CLASS AS E23 AND E27, AND THEY ARE NOW FOUR INSTANCES IN ONE DAY, EACH FOUND INDEPENDENTLY: the reset archived registers and nothing swept the workflows, guards and skills that read them. [!] UPPER BOUND, EXPLICITLY NOT A DEFECT COUNT: scanning 562 source files under .github/workflows, scripts/ci, scripts/ops and .claude/skills (pycache excluded) for repo-relative path literals, 137 distinct paths DO NOT EXIST on disk, and 34 workflows name at least one. That number is NOT 137 bugs -- many are files the naming workflow PRODUCES (the econ-calendar and macro backfills are the obvious ones), so the deliverable is a TRIAGE separating `reads a file that must pre-exist` from `writes it`, then fixing the first set. Do not sweep on the raw count. SCOPE: fix the three named failures first, since those are observed red, then triage the rest and file what is left. [!] ================ E29 BUILD LANE, 2026-09-22 — PR #12719 (DRAFT, landing: hold) ================ [!] WORK-DIGEST'S CAUSE IS NOW ESTABLISHED, and the row was right to refuse to guess it: it is NOT the same as the other two. `python3 scripts/ops/work_digest.py --self-test` fails check 10 (`every declared source exists on disk`) naming FIVE archived registers -- docs/claude/OPEN-ITEMS.json and ALL FOUR docs/claude/*-review-backlog.json. Established by RUNNING the self-test on the checkout, not by reading a log. [!] AND THE RED CI IS THE SMALLER HALF OF THAT FINDING: five of the digest's six declared sources have read `absent` on EVERY run from the reset onward, so the work digest has been structurally blind to five-sixths of its inputs while reporting itself healthy. The three causes re-verified by running each failing step on the checkout rather than trusting this row. [!] DISPOSITIONS, EACH DECIDED RATHER THAN DEFAULTED TO REPAIR. (1) merge-claim-audit RETIRED: it audits the merge-slot claim protocol on the coordination board the reset retired. The repair WAS available and was rejected on its merits -- board_pointer.py accepts `board_state: "retired"`, so a tombstone pointer makes the self-test pass; that is a workflow running on every merge to say `there is no board`. Its stated purpose was to build ONE number (how often an unclaimed merge coincides with a real collision) to decide whether to enforce, and with no board that number can never be collected. (2) reconcile-open-prs RETIRED: its register is archived. (3) work-digest REPAIRED, not retired: the five dead sources are cut and MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json -- THE register under the reset's own `one register` model -- remains, so the digest now watches exactly the surface the operating model says work lives on. Triggers are COMMENTED OUT rather than the files deleted: check_workflow_catalog.py pins every workflow to a catalogue row in both directions, and each file's rationale is a decision record. Both catalogue rows updated. [!] THE 14 OPEN PRs ARE ANSWERED, AND THE ANSWER IS CLOSE THEM, NOT MERGE THEM -- MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. #12451…#12511, opened 2026-09-17T15:30Z … 2026-09-18T04:47Z. (a) Every branch is cut from a PRE-RESET main: `git diff --stat main <branch>` gives 1,055 files / 315,876 deletions on the newest (#12511) and 1,190 / 394,616 on the oldest (#12451), so MERGING ANY ONE REVERTS THE OPERATING RESET WHOLESALE. (b) Nothing is lost by closing them: their only payload is OPEN-PRS.json (the job's `paths:` names that file alone) and it is strictly STALER than the archived copy -- branch 9 open / 114 settled against the archive's 12 / 118, and #12400, the one number the branch has that the archive's open_prs lacks, sits in the archive's settled_prs, i.e. already reconciled. (c) The known drop hazard does NOT apply: sweep_stale_automation_prs.py warns that closing a WORK-DIGEST PR drops queued pending-pings.jsonl rows; these are not work-digest PRs and carry no ping payload. [!] I DID NOT CLOSE THEM. Fourteen closes are outward-facing and the lane's dispatch says push, open a draft, update the row, STOP. Filed as PI-20260922-RECONCILE-OPEN-PRS-14-STRANDED-PRS-NEED-CLOSING-NOT-MERGING. MANAGER: this is the one action this row leaves undone that has a live footgun behind it. [!] THE SHAPE FIX, WHICH OUTLASTS ALL THREE. `open_pr_record.read_record()` reported an ABSENT file as `(None, readable=True)` -- `the register is gone` and `the register read fine` were the SAME VALUE, which is why the failure arrived as a stack trace instead of as a finding. Added `read_record_state()` returning `absent | read | unreadable`, with read_record() now defined in terms of it so the two cannot drift, and a FOURTH verdict `register_absent` on the reconciler that EXITS 0 AND SAYS THE FILE IS MISSING. A fourth state rather than a flavour of could_not_look, deliberately: absent and present-but-unreadable are opposite findings with opposite remedies. [!] A JOB THAT EXITS CLEAN HAVING SILENTLY DONE NOTHING WOULD HAVE BEEN THE WORSE FIX, so the test asserts absent AGAINST A PRESENT-AND-EMPTY POSITIVE CONTROL rather than merely that the crash is gone. [!] TWO DEFECTS FOUND BY CONTROLS WHILE FIXING, NEITHER BY INSPECTION, AND BOTH WORTH THE ROW. (i) read_record's `path=RECORD_PATH` default BOUND AT IMPORT, so repointing RECORD_PATH was silently ignored and the function read the original file while appearing to honour the override -- caught only because the new test carried a positive control. Now resolved at call time. (ii) tests/test_work_digest.py::test_editing_a_backlog_row_without_closing_it_is_activity had gone VACUOUS AND STAYED GREEN: it asserts `events == []`, which an unwatched path satisfies for entirely the wrong reason. The differ tests now declare their own fixture registers so they cannot pass because the roster moved, and the roster test itself was rewritten -- it USED TO REQUIRE OPEN-ITEMS.json, which is how a roster test outlives its roster. [!] THE TRIAGE, AND IT CHANGES THE PROPOSED REMEDY RATHER THAN CONFIRMING IT. The 137 figure is an upper bound and re-running that shape is NOT a usable detector: my own first pass produced 216 and was dominated by noise -- an extension-ordering bug splitting .jsonl as .json, self-test fixture literals, docstring prose, and files the naming workflow PRODUCES. THE DECIDABLE SIGNAL IS NARROWER: a path the reset ARCHIVED that a live source still names. MEASURED: 289 paths archived and still absent, 40 of them STILL NAMED by live sources under .github/workflows, scripts/ci, scripts/ops and .claude/skills -- health-review-backlog.json 31 namers, OPEN-ITEMS.json 25, ml-review-backlog.json 25, performance-review-backlog.json 23, SESSIONS.json 16, research-review-backlog.json 15, board-pointer.json 12. [!] THE PROBE HAS ONE TRAP AND IT SILENTLY REPORTS ALL-CLEAR: the reset RENAMED files into docs/archive/, so `git diff --diff-filter=D` returns ZERO and only `--no-renames` sees them. I hit that and caught it on a positive control. PROPOSED REMEDY: one guard keyed on archived-and-still-referenced, shipped REPORT-ONLY against a declared baseline that shrinks, NEVER blocking -- 40 paths across ~60 files would go red on every PR at once and a guard nobody can go green against gets waived rather than satisfied. IT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT ALL FOUR OF THE DAY'S INSTANCES: E23 (and its three unfixed sibling skills), E27, and all three of this row's workflows. Filed as PI-20260922-ARCHIVED-REGISTERS-STILL-READ-BY-40-PATHS-ACROSS-LIVE-CI-SOURCES. [!] NOT DONE, STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED. (1) The board family -- board-heartbeat.yml, board-post.yml, board-rotate.yml, scope-overlap-audit.yml, pr-close.yml -- still resolves through the absent pointer. NONE is red, and that is NOT because they are healthy: parsing each `on:` block, heartbeat and scope-overlap are workflow_dispatch ONLY, and board-post/board-rotate fire only on pushes to automation/board-*/** which nothing writes now. They are DORMANT, and each goes red the moment it is dispatched. That is one decision about the family, not five patches. (2) PIPELINE.jsonl is still not a digest source -- it is append-only JSONL, not a keyed register, so _items_at() cannot diff it, and until that lands a pipeline item coming due produces NO PING. (3) Six modules still call the two-state read_record() and treat absent as empty; the collapse is now pinned by a test so a future edit has to mean it. [!] VERIFICATION, run on the checkout: work_digest --self-test PASS (was FAIL), with a NEGATIVE CONTROL -- restoring a retired register to disk makes new check 11b FAIL, removing it restores PASS, so the new check has teeth. reconcile_open_prs.py --json now prints state=register_absent, exit 0, naming the file and the archive path. check_workflow_catalog.py OK (143 workflows, both directions). Both retired workflows parse to {'workflow_dispatch': None} -- verified by loading the YAML, not by reading the diff. 801 tests pass across tests/ops/, test_work_digest*, test_handoff_check, test_open_prs_settled_regress, test_merge_slot_state. run_guards.py exits 0 against the commit range, and the one COULD-NOT-RUN guard (layer-guard, missing import-linter) was installed and re-run separately: 6 contracts kept, 0 broken. items.title: The paper books' P&L is mostly NOT measured, which is the stage that exists to measure realized cost
items.note:
MERGED 2026-09-24 as PR #12735 (Tier-3, operator-approved in chat 2026-09-24: 'Approve -- land it'). `landed_unproven`, NOT `done`: the fix changes when one column is written and nothing has yet shown a row upgrade. THE OBSERVATION THAT CLOSES THIS ROW is PI-20260922-54WQNHJX-0001 -- a `pairs_*` close carrying exit_price_source `exchange_fill` AND paper pnlCoverage above 0.30 (floor today 0.2236). If it does not move, the fix is inert and the next suspect is exit_from_fills' qty/window match on pairs legs, not the sweep scope.

PRIOR NOTE ----------------------------------------------------------------
DIAGNOSED AND FIXED (fix HELD for Tier-2 approval) 2026-09-22 by the E30 lane, session_017mdYduTwtyVPXU54wqNHJx, branch claude/e30-pairs-pnl-measured-0922.

[1] THE DENOMINATOR, which this row said must be established FIRST. READ FROM THE CODE, not inferred: provenance.coverage() divides MEASURED by `total`, and _pnl_provenance.block_for_rows sets total=len(rows) -- i.e. EVERY row in the population, so FABRICATED and UNVERIFIED rows are in the denominator and in neither published count. MEASURED 2026-09-22T12:36:53Z, GET https://ict-bot.duckdns.org/api/bot/stats: paper pnlCoverage 0.2236, M=267, E=664. Population (dashboard.py::_pnl_provenance_for): status='closed' AND is_backtest=0 AND pnl IS NOT NULL AND account_class='paper' AND strategy_name!='orphan_adopt' AND reconcile_status!='superseded', n=1,194 -> M 267 (22.4%) / E 664 (55.6%) / F 128 (10.7%) / U 135 (11.3%). REAL: n=431 -> M 329 / E 20 / F 4 / U 78, cov 0.7633. So 'the paper book is 78% estimated' is FALSE and must not be requoted; it is 55.6% estimated with a further 22% carrying no usable anchor at all. INSTRUMENT VALIDATED: I pulled the whole live trades table (n=6,059) via /api/diag/journal and re-classified it with src.runtime.provenance.classify_pnl -- it reproduces both published figures to the digit (0.7633/329/20 and 0.2236/267/664), so every decomposition below rests on the endpoint's own classifier.

[2] THE ANSWER TO THE THREE-WAY QUESTION IS (1): THE FILLS ARE MEASURABLE AND WE NEVER WIRED THIS PATH TO THE READ. Not a venue limit. Positive control, same account and same 14 days: 48 non-pairs bybit_1 closes resolved to exit_price_source='exchange_fill' (MEASURED) off the demo venue's own fills. The gap is one order path. MEASURED over the full table: 365 pairs_* closes exist, ALL on bybit_1, and **0 of 365 have ever classified MEASURED**. 0/365 is a structural exclusion, not a flaky lookup.

[3] ROOT CAUSE, one line and verified end to end. The bot's PnL-resolution contract (stated in order_monitor._sweep_pending_pnl_from_bybit's own docstring) is: CLOSE PATHS LEAVE `pnl` NULL AND THE SWEEPS FILL IT WITH BROKER TRUTH ON A LATER TICK. BOTH sweeps select on `AND pnl IS NULL` (_sweep_pending_pnl_from_bybit, _sweep_local_pnl_for_unpriced). The M22 pairs executor -- an ISOLATED 2-leg order path that never goes through multi_account_execute or the monitor's close paths -- computed and WROTE `pnl` at close time, under a comment claiming 'broker-truth sweep may refine bybit later'. THAT COMMENT WAS FALSE: writing the number did not race the sweep, it removed the row from the sweep's scope permanently. Everything downstream was already built and correct and needed NO change: clients.account_closed_pnl_for_trade's DEMO branch resolves from the exchange-fills store (#8111); the broker sweep stamps exit_price_source from the record and explicitly declines to relabel a pairs_* exit_reason (its guard 2 NAMES this path -- the author anticipated these rows arriving, and they never did); ict-exchange-fills-pull.timer is HOURLY to serve the 6h _LOCAL_PNL_BROKER_DEFER_MS window, and I OBSERVED it active on the live VM at 12:37Z with last_trigger 12:21:11Z.

[4] THE FIX: stop writing pnl/pnl_percent at the pairs close site so the row enters the contract every other close path already follows. exit_price and the candle_at_close stamp still written -- both are true at that instant and the broker sweep overwrites them together if a fill lands; if none ever does the local fallback prices the row from that same value, i.e. TODAY's outcome. So the change can upgrade a row and can NEVER downgrade one. UPPER BOUND over the live population -- NOT a prediction, and labelled so nobody quotes it as one: IF every one of the 365 pairs rows resolved to a fill, paper pnlCoverage would be 0.5293 and bybit_1 0.5657. Some fraction will not match (exit_from_fills refuses on qty tolerance and on its open/close window, and it refuses rather than approximating), and I did not measure that fraction. The floor is today's 0.2236, because the change can only upgrade a row. Tests: tests/test_pairs_close_provenance.py -- the old assertion `pnl == 20.0` was PINNING the defect and is replaced, plus a real-sqlite positive+negative control that a priced row is EXCLUDED by the sweep predicate, plus a source-read guard that both sweeps still gate on `pnl IS NULL` so a future edit there cannot silently strand this. 128 passed / 0 failed across every test file importing pairs_executor; 100 passed across the db-integrity + invariant suites.

[5] STATUS: MERGED? NO. PR #12735, opened as a draft. Declared TIER-3: I first declared Tier-2 (journal write path) and pr-landing-guard correctly answered that the diff touches a path it names Tier-3 (src/units/strategies/), so I took the stricter tier rather than arguing the guard down -- under-declaring a tier is the PR #1358 failure class. Landing is HELD for the operator/manager. NOTHING IS DEPLOYED AND NOTHING IS OBSERVED. The observation that would close this row is filed as PI-20260922-54WQNHJX-0001 (clears when a pairs_* close carries exchange_fill AND paper pnlCoverage > 0.30). The residual I did NOT root-cause -- non-pairs paper coverage is still only 0.3221 (n=829) vs the real book's 0.7633, so the pairs fix is the largest block and NOT the whole answer -- is filed as PI-20260922-54WQNHJX-0002. OPENED 2026-09-22 by the manager. The 2026-09-22 /health-review graded `data_validity` as `watch` and named these figures, but the finding was left in the review JSON and NEVER became a row -- so by the close-out skill's own test it was not filed. This row is that filing. MEASURED LIVE by me at 2026-09-22T09:1x from GET /api/bot/stats, and the numbers have MOVED since the review (paper 264/658 -> 266/661), so this is ongoing, not a stale snapshot: real book pnlCoverage 0.7633 with pnlMeasuredCount 329 / pnlEstimatedCount 20; PAPER book pnlCoverage 0.2235 with pnlMeasuredCount 266 / pnlEstimatedCount 661. [!] WHY THIS IS NOT COSMETIC: under the promotion ladder, Stage 1 (bybit_1 / alpaca_paper) exists to answer exactly one question -- `do the mechanics work, and does REALIZED COST match what the backtest assumed`. A book whose P&L is predominantly ESTIMATED cannot answer a question about REALIZED cost. So Gate 1's instrument may be reading its own reconstruction rather than the venue, and E3's whole point was that the backtests were fee-only and optimistic by an unknown amount. If the paper book that is supposed to check that assumption is itself largely estimated, the check is weaker than anyone has stated. [!] WHAT I DID NOT ESTABLISH, STATED SO NOBODY QUOTES A NUMBER I DID NOT VERIFY: the DENOMINATOR of pnlCoverage. 266/(266+661) = 0.287, which is NOT the 0.2235 the field reports, so coverage is computed over a larger population than measured+estimated -- there is at least a third bucket (plausibly UNVERIFIED per src/runtime/provenance.py, which the rules say is never folded into measured). Do not restate 'the paper book is 78% estimated' until that denominator is read from the code. FIRST TASK OF THIS ROW IS TO ESTABLISH IT. [!] THEN: find out WHY the paper legs' fills are not measured when the real book's are (broker fill records absent for paper accounts? a different write path? an ingest that never ran?), and say whether it is fixable or structural. If structural, the honest outcome is a stated limit on what Gate 1 can conclude -- which is worth more than a fix that is not available. [!] CLOSE-OUT TRUE-STATE PASS, 2026-09-22T18:4xZ, manager session_01XQhayAHWdrSYv8jN54P2HH. Was `queued` with no PR link while the work sat finished and green in #12735. The lane (session_017mdYduTwtyVPXU54wqNHJx) is WALLED on an unattended permission prompt with staged work; a human must clear it, and the manager did not answer it on the operator's behalf. Its merge conflict was already resolved and pushed by the manager, so the PR does not need the lane. [!] OPERATOR APPROVAL GIVEN 2026-09-24 (Tier-3, explicit). Asked as one of four decisions, with the tier and the substance both stated: Tier-3 by path (src/units/strategies/pairs_executor.py), bookkeeping in substance (entry, exit decision, exit price, exit reason and the close order byte-identical; it stops the close pre-filling the pnl COLUMN so the broker-truth sweeps can reach the row). The operator chose 'Approve - land it'. The manager lands it; the lane declared the stricter tier itself rather than arguing pr-landing-guard down, and that judgement stands as correct. [!] NOT `done` ON THE MERGE: PI-20260922-54WQNHJX-0001 is the observation that closes this row - a pairs_* close carrying `exchange_fill` AND paper pnlCoverage above 0.30. If coverage does not move, the fix is INERT and the next suspect is exit_from_fills' qty/window match, not the sweep scope.

[!] WITHDRAWN 2026-09-24 — THE 'ONLY A HUMAN CAN CLEAR IT' CLAIM ABOVE IS FALSE AND WAS NEVER TESTED. It is left in place rather than deleted so the correction is legible against what it corrects. FALSIFIED by one attempt: interrupt_session on the walled lane, then a message delivered through a create_trigger with persistent_session_id set to it. MEASURED on session_017mdYduTwtyVPXU54wqNHJx, which had shown no activity for 39 hours (last 2026-09-22T13:51:41Z): the trigger fired 2026-09-24T05:32:00Z and get_session shows a turn at 05:32:42Z ending status_bucket COMPLETED, reporting a clean tree, nothing staged or unpushed, and that its own staged_files:true flag was a FALSE ALARM. The operator's words, recorded because the correction is theirs: 'you can definitely take care of those permissions instead of me'.
[!] AND THE NARROWER FORM, because over-claiming the correction would repeat the original error in the other direction: ONE case establishes this, not two. The same technique was also aimed at session_01R9WFrBK1sbBcpTYgBmvG1q and it did reply, but that session runs a 6-hourly cron that would have woken it anyway, and its own 06:44Z heartbeat states it 'was not itself blocked on anything at the time'. A session that was going to wake regardless is not evidence that a message clears a wall. What is established: a message CAN move a session reporting BLOCKED. What is NOT established: that it always can, or what distinguishes the cases. Do not read this as a guarantee; read it as a probe that must be RUN rather than assumed either way — the original defect was asserting the limit for two days without ever attempting it once.

items.note: OPERATOR DIRECTIVE 2026-09-22, verbatim: 'there does need to be some convergence here... the state is still representing something that's incorrect, so either the bybit or the breakout accounts need to have the correct adjustments based on the results we see from running those tests.' AGREED. [!] THE INCOHERENCE IS NOT WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE. It is not that prop carries a leg bybit_2 lacks. The roster reflects HISTORY, not evidence; the prop/bybit asymmetry is a symptom, not the disease. [!] A NAIVE RULE WOULD BE ACTIVELY DANGEROUS, which is why the operator has to set the second half. items.title: The prop bar is an EXPECTED-VALUE question, not a drawdown-avoidance one — and the corpus cannot answer it
items.note: OPERATOR DIRECTIVE 2026-09-22, and it REPLACES the bar I proposed an hour earlier: 'it's ok if there is ever breach, the idea is that we want to promote strategies that create a portfolio that we would statistically expect to produce a profit (over the initial account cost of about 1%) before the account dies - that is the basis for building the prop portfolio.' [!] SO THE PROP BAR IS: E[profit before the account dies] > the account cost. Breach is an ACCEPTED, EXPECTED outcome -- the cost of the bet -- not a failure to prevent. This is a ruin-WITH-PAYOFF problem and the quantity is a survival-weighted expected value. [!] I PROPOSED `max_dd_r < 4.0` AS THE PROP BAR AND THAT IS WITHDRAWN. It is a risk-avoidance constraint on a problem that is not about avoiding risk, and it would have refused exactly the high-variance legs this account exists to buy a lottery ticket on. [!] AND MY SUPPORTING ARGUMENT WAS ALSO WRONG, WHICH IS THE MORE USEFUL CORRECTION: I said 1.5% sizing against a 6% static DD 'makes almost nothing fit'. THE BARRIER RATIO IS INVARIANT TO SIZING. At risk_pct 1.5: DD room 6%/1.5% = 4.0R, profit target 10%/1.5% = 6.67R, ratio 1.667. At 0.5%: 12.0R and 20.0R, ratio 1.667. Both barriers scale together, so cutting risk_pct does not change the ratio at all; it helps only through the second-order effect that more trades to either barrier let positive drift accumulate against variance. With trend_donchian_eth_prop's expectancy of +0.042R/trade, +6.67R is ~159 trades of drift against 4R of room, so variance dominates heavily -- whether smaller sizing raises P(success) is a COMPUTABLE QUESTION and I should not have asserted it in either direction. [!] TWO FEATURES OF THIS ACCOUNT MAKE THE EV BETTER THAN A NAIVE ABSORBING-BARRIER MODEL, both CONFIRMED in config/prop_rulesets/breakout.yaml: (1) drawdown_type is STATIC -- 'off the STARTING balance; NOT trailing and NOT locked/raised on payout' -- so every dollar of profit is PERMANENT cushion and the account gets monotonically safer as it wins; survival is front-loaded. (2) min_trading_days 0 and max_eval_days null -- no time pressure, can clear in one trade, so there is no forced-pace term. STRUCTURE: $45 (0.9% of the $5,000 account) buys a shot at +10% ($500) before -6% ($300); clearing converts to a funded account paying 80/20 on subsequent profits under the same static limits. So E[value] = P(clear eval) x E[lifetime payout | funded] - $45. [!] SELECTION CRITERION, AND IT IS NOT net_R: maximise P(reaching the target before the floor). A leg with LOWER expectancy but tighter loss clustering beats a higher-expectancy leg whose losses arrive in lumps. And it is a PORTFOLIO question, not a per-leg one -- legs whose drawdowns are uncorrelated smooth the path to the barrier. [!] NOTE THE ASYMMETRY WITH R8: the operator chose NO concentration cap for bybit_2, and correlation is nonetheless load-bearing HERE, in the opposite direction -- on prop it is not a risk limit, it is the mechanism that raises P(survival). [!] THIS RETROACTIVELY EXPLAINS THE _prop EXIT GEOMETRY, which nobody wrote down: tp_r 6.0 vs 50.0, trail_mult 3.5 vs 5.0, stale_exit_bars 12, trail_decay_stall_bars 10 / tight_mult 1.8. Capping the upside at 6R and cutting dead trades is exactly what raises P(hit +6.67R before -4R) at the cost of expectancy. Someone built the right thing for the right reason and recorded neither, so it read as an arbitrary divergence between prop and bybit -- which is what the operator asked about today. [!] THE ACTUAL GAP IS A MISSING MEASUREMENT, NOT A MISSING CONSTRAINT: MEASURED 2026-09-22, none of the 52 records under comms/strategy_evidence/ carries a per-trade R series or ANY path statistic (keys are basis, config_fingerprint, cost_stack, coverage_state, decision_rule, expectancy_r_oos, fold_detail, folds, folds_positive, n_trades_oos, net_r_oos, net_r_oos_fee_only, omitted_levers, param_selection_provenance, window_days -- no drawdown of any kind), and scripts/ci/check_roster_promotion_evidence.py never reads one. fold_detail gives only a per-fold SUM over months, which is not an equity path. DELIVERABLE: emit the per-trade OOS R series (or a sufficient path summary) so P(target before floor) is computable per leg AND per candidate portfolio, then register that rule BEFORE using it. [!] WHAT I COMPUTED FROM fold_detail AND ITS LIMIT, kept because it is what prompted the reframe: 13 of the 42 legs with fold detail have a single fold worse than -4R, and BOTH legs live on breakout_1 are among them while both are marked `pass` (trend_donchian_eth_prop worst fold -5.3884R on total +7.13). That is NOT evidence of a breach -- a fold's net_R is a sum over months, not a contiguous drawdown -- and under this row's bar it would not be disqualifying even if it were. It is evidence only that the bar cannot see the path.

PRIOR NOTE ----------------------------------------------------------------
BUILT 2026-09-22, PR #12738 (draft, Tier-2 hold). THE ROW'S DIAGNOSIS WAS RE-VERIFIED FROM THE CODE RATHER THAN TRUSTED, and it was right on all three counts: /api/bot/config's field is `yaml_mode`; build_status computes `live` as _read_live_per_account(accounts_yaml) and `strategies` as _read_strategy_names(strategies_yaml), both of which open and parse the YAML. [!] ONE THING THE ROW DID NOT SAY, AND IT CHANGES THE SHAPE OF THE FIX: what the process holds is ASYMMETRIC. MEASURED 2026-09-22 by reading src/strategy_registry.py, src/runtime/pipeline.py:364, src/units/accounts/__init__.py and src/core/coordinator.py:2795 -- strategy_registry._cache is populated on the first load and NEVER invalidated, and pipeline.STRATEGY_ROSTER resolves at IMPORT, so strategies.yaml needs a RESTART; load_accounts() re-opens accounts.yaml on every call (once per tick via main._resolve_tick_symbols, once per dispatch via multi_account_execute), so that half converges on the next tick. A single `is it current?` boolean would have been wrong for one of them, so the surface reports PER FILE. [!] WHAT SHIPPED: src/runtime/loaded_config.py (producer; two three-state contracts now registered with collapsed-state-guard, which is clean at 50) -- `process_state` observed/not_written/unreadable keeps `we could not look` out of `the trader holds nothing` (`loaded` is null, never []), and `reload_state` current/pending_reload/unknown is the field that turns `deployed` into an observation. Each loader stamps the path, a sha256 over THE EXACT BYTES IT PARSED, a UTC timestamp, and the values it resolved (per-account dry_run read off the RiskManager the process built, never re-derived from the file). runtime_status.json gains a `process` block; schema_version stays 1 because the addition is additive and the reader detects it by PRESENCE. Served at GET /api/bot/runtime-config (Tier 1, read-only) and by scripts/ops/verify_running_roster.py. [!] THE THREE FALSE CLAIMS ARE CORRECTED IN PLACE AND THE CAPABILITY WAS BUILT RATHER THAN THE CLAIM DELETED, as the row required -- and there was a THIRD the row did not name: /api/bot/strategies' `loaded` column was documented as `the names the running process actually loaded` and is a file read. It keeps its meaning (the SPA consumes it) and gains a tri-state `held_by_process` beside it, where None is not False. [!] VERIFIED AGAINST LIVE DATA, not only fixtures: vm-diag-snapshot relay, issue #12734 / run 35729811659, captured 2026-09-22T12:52:33Z -- the live artifact carries schema_version 1 and NO `process` key, and fed to the new reader it returns `not_written` with `loaded: None`. That is a live positive control for the state that matters most. [!] READ-ONLY AND FENCED: the stamp inside load_accounts is reached from Coordinator.multi_account_execute and is wrapped so a failure to OBSERVE degrades to `no stamp` and dispatch continues byte-for-byte. Nothing in the order path consults any of it, and nothing may be made to. FOUND 2026-09-22 by the manager at close-out, while trying to establish what would move R2 and B2 from `landed_unproven` to `done`. It turns out nothing can, today. [!] READ FROM THE CODE, NOT THE PROSE. (1) /api/bot/config's per-account mode field is literally named `yaml_mode` -- honest naming, and it means the payload reports the FILE on the VM. (2) The payload's `trading_mode` block carries a note asserting `live_per_account is the pipeline's runtime view`, which is STRONGER THAN WHAT THE CODE DOES: that value comes from runtime_status.json, written by the live pipeline on every tick via src/web/runtime_status.py::build_status -- and build_status computes it as `_read_live_per_account(accounts_yaml)`, which OPENS AND PARSES config/accounts.yaml. (3) The same file's `strategies` field is `_read_strategy_names(strategies_yaml)`, which opens and parses config/strategies.yaml. [!] SO THE ONE ARTIFACT THE TRADING PROCESS ITSELF WRITES REPORTS THE CONFIG FILE, NOT ITS OWN LOADED STATE. `the pipeline wrote it` is not `the pipeline is using it`, and every reader has been taking the first for the second. The genuine process facts in that file are bot_uptime_s and git_sha; the roster and the per-account mode are not among them. [!] WHY THIS IS NOT PEDANTRY, ON A LIVE-MONEY SYSTEM: a roster edit is not live until the trader reloads config. Between the merge and that reload, a leg the evidence bar just CUT is still trading real money, and there is no way to tell -- every surface shows the cut. R2 (Tier-3, 4 legs cut from bybit_2 / bybit_portfolio / breakout_1) and B2 (alpaca_portfolio 14 -> 2) are both `landed_unproven` for exactly this reason, and both would close the moment such a surface existed. Same defect class as E22: a reading surface structurally unable to express the state that matters. [!] DELIVERABLE: make runtime_status.json (or a sibling) report the roster the process HOLDS -- pipeline.STRATEGIES and the resolved per-account effective_dry -- beside the file-read values, with the two DISTINGUISHABLE and a `config_reloaded_at` stamp so `pending_reload` is a readable state rather than an invisible one. Then fix /api/bot/config's note, which currently claims a runtime view it does not have. Tier 2: it changes what a live service publishes. [!] DO NOT `fix` this by deleting the note and leaving the gap -- the note is wrong because the capability is missing, not the other way round. items.title: The verification mapping — how we establish what is ACTUALLY trading, layer by layer, with which layers we do not have
items.note:
DONE 2026-09-24 -- merged AND observed. OBSERVED 2026-09-24T06:34:28Z. GET https://ict-bot.duckdns.org/api/bot/runtime-config (the served twin of scripts/ops/verify_running_roster.py, both shipped by #12738) returned HTTP 200 with process_state `observed`, verdict CURRENT, and reload_state `current` for BOTH accounts_yaml and strategies_yaml -- loaded_digest == on_disk_digest (accounts sha256:797eca02..., strategies sha256:2669a35d...). pid 4137367, boot 2026-09-24T06:25:27Z, last_tick 06:34:20Z, tick_age 8.1s, bot_ticking true, git_sha f8ef1db5b. f8ef1db5b contains a66a1eca2 (#12738) -- checked with `git merge-base --is-ancestor`, not assumed. The restart came from system-action `pull-and-deploy` (issue #12797, run 35964326891, wrapper exit 0): HEAD f7a052513 -> f8ef1db5b, ict-trader-live.service and ict-web-api.service both bounced at 06:25:28Z.

E32's own rule ('a Tier-3 roster change is done when layer 4 agrees with layer 6') is what was read, not inferred: layer 4 (the process's held roster) and layer 5 (the files on disk) agree by digest, and layer 6 (the checkout's git sha) is f8ef1db5b. The three layers this tool does NOT answer (1-3: broker positions, closed trades, decision-level emissions) are unchanged and still carry their own caveats -- docs/reference/verifying-what-is-trading.md.

PRIOR NOTE ----------------------------------------------------------------
OPERATOR DIRECTIVE 2026-09-22: 'we need to be able to verify what's actually trading... it's being operated from our VM, which means there is a single source of truth -- whatever the VM is using is de facto the single source of truth for what's actually trading. And if we can't verify that, then we need to build the mechanism to verify that... there's no reason that that question should just stay open-ended.' AGREED. This row is the mapping, and it exists because I tried to verify R2's cut this session and COULD NOT. [!] THE SIX LAYERS, IN DESCENDING AUTHORITY, EACH WITH WHETHER IT IS READABLE TODAY. (1) THE BROKER -- what positions and orders actually exist at Bybit/Alpaca. Highest authority; nothing on the VM can override it. Readable via /api/bot/positions (unrealizedPnlSource distinguishes broker truth from a local mark) and /api/bot/pnl/broker-truth. AVAILABLE. (2) REALISED BEHAVIOUR -- what the system has actually closed. /api/bot/trades/closed, keyed on `pattern` and `account`. AVAILABLE, and it is the only layer that proves a leg TRADED rather than was configured to. (3) DECISION-LEVEL EMISSIONS -- /api/bot/order-packages and /api/bot/signals. PARTIALLY BROKEN, see the measurements below. (4) THE PROCESS'S LOADED STATE -- pipeline.STRATEGIES and the resolved per-account effective_dry. NOT AVAILABLE AT ALL; this is row E31, and it is the layer the operator's question actually needs. (5) THE FILE ON THE VM -- /api/bot/config, whose mode field is honestly named `yaml_mode`. AVAILABLE, and it is what every reader has been mistaking for layer 4. (6) GIT main. AVAILABLE, and the furthest from the truth. [!] MEASURED THIS SESSION, AND THE HEADLINE IS THAT BEHAVIOURAL VERIFICATION CANNOT WORK FOR A REAL-MONEY BOOK AT TODAY'S TRADE RATE. Population: the 200 most recent closed trades, closedAt 2026-09-13T20:55:29Z -> 2026-09-22T08:48:49Z, about 9 days. Of those, 199 are PAPER and 1 is REAL MONEY -- a single bybit_2/xrp_pullback_2h trade closed 2026-09-14T18:21:48Z, EIGHT DAYS AGO. Trades closed after R2's cut: 2, both bybit_1 (paper), both ict_scalp_*. So when I asked `did any cut leg trade after the cut`, the answer was NONE -- and THE POSITIVE CONTROL FAILED, because no real-money leg traded after the cut either. A negative from a probe whose positive control is silent proves nothing. At a base rate near 0.1 real-money trades/day you would wait weeks for a behavioural answer, and layer 4 is therefore NOT OPTIONAL -- it is the only layer that can answer the question for real money on any useful timescale. [!] TWO DEFECTS FOUND IN LAYER 3 WHILE BUILDING THIS, BOTH THE COLLAPSED-STATE CLASS. (a) /api/bot/order-packages?limit=201 returns `rows: []` with `count: 0` -- NOT an error and NOT a clamp to the 200 cap. An over-limit request is INDISTINGUISHABLE from `there is no data`, on a read surface the SPA uses. Verified by bisection: limit 50/100/200 return 50/100/200; 201 and 250 return 0. (b) /api/bot/order-packages' newest row is 2026-09-18T15:16:46Z, four days stale, while closed trades exist from today -- so the decision-level surface is NOT tracking what the system is actually doing. (c) /api/bot/signals returns 0 rows under EVERY shape tried (bare, limit=5, limit=50, hours=720, limit=50&hours=2000 -- an 83-day window). I could NOT establish whether that is `no signals` or `a broken read`, and I am not guessing; that distinction is the same defect this row exists to remove. [!] DELIVERABLE: a single documented procedure -- one command or endpoint -- that answers `what is the running trader actually trading right now, and does it match main?`, returning each layer separately with its own read-state, NEVER collapsing `we could not look` into `nothing found`, and REFUSING to return a verdict when the positive control for a behavioural layer is silent. Depends on E31 for layer 4. [!] AND A RULE THAT FALLS OUT OF IT: a Tier-3 roster change is not `done` when the file changes; it is done when layer 4 agrees with layer 6. R2 and B2 are both sitting in exactly that gap right now. [!] OPERATOR CORRECTION 2026-09-22, and it narrows this row: 'the roster is not a behaviour-observable fact, it is a LIST-observable fact based on the list that is the single source of truth. Just because something's not trading doesn't mean it's not on the roster -- it could just be sidelined. The only problem we would notice is if we see something trading that's NOT on the roster.' CORRECT, and it means I built the wrong check first. The roster question is answered by READING THE LIST THE VM IS CONFIGURED WITH, not by watching for trades; absence of trading is not absence from the roster, and my behavioural probe was testing a proposition the roster does not make. THE LAYER-2 CHECK IS THEREFORE AN INVERSE ANOMALY DETECTOR, NOT A CONFIRMATION: alert when a leg that is NOT on an account's list closes a trade on it. That is a positive assertion, it needs no positive control, and it fires on the thing that actually matters. items.title: Derive the settled-evidence cut-points from the arm's own purpose (expected armings per horizon), not from a picked share
items.note: [!] ID CORRECTED 2026-09-22 by the manager: this row was filed as E42 from a branch cut before #12725 landed, and E42 was taken on main by an unrelated row (the accounts.yaml symbol list). Two rows sharing an id is the collision E13 built a check for one level up, and it would have merged as a silent clobber rather than a conflict. Renamed to E47; no content changed. SPLIT OUT OF E41 BY THE LANE, 2026-09-22, so the flag could land today. The operator REJECTED the two proposed cut-points, verbatim: "we need data-backed values, not arbitrary ones (otherwise what's the point of the arm in the first place?)". PR #12745 lands the flag WITHOUT them -- it emits `settled_*` only where the verdict is invariant across the still-open cut-point band -- and this row is the derivation that closes the gap. [!] THE SPECIFICATION IS THE OPERATOR'S OWN PARENTHESIS. An arm exists to modify exits on trades that REACH arm_r, so the quantity that matters is not a bare share but EXPECTED ARMINGS PER HORIZON at the leg's own trade rate. A 5% reach share is ~10 armings/year on a leg trading 200 times a year and ~0.3 on a leg trading 6 times a year; those are different facts and one share-threshold cannot separate them. That also makes the threshold PER LEG, which is why the current band has to be leg-independent and therefore weak. [!] PROPOSED DERIVATION, written out so this needs no re-deriving. (1) expected_armings(leg, horizon) = reach_share * trades_per_horizon(leg). (2) trades_per_horizon is MEASURABLE TODAY and needs no new instrument: every comms/strategy_evidence/runs/<run>/<leg>__bt.json carries `total_trades` with `data_start` and `data_end`, so trades/day falls straight out; the same files already back the k/n in config/lever_reachability.json. (3) settled_inert when the CI-HIGH share implies FEWER THAN ONE expected arming over the horizon -- i.e. even the optimistic end of the interval predicts the lever never fires in that window. settled_reachable when the CI-LOW implies at least N. (4) [!] THE HORIZON AND N ARE THE PART THAT IS STILL UNDERIVED, AND THEY MUST COME FROM SOMETHING REAL -- the demotion-review cadence, the corpus span, the e35 re-check interval -- with the file saying WHERE EACH CAME FROM. Do not substitute a round number; that is the exact failure this row exists to correct. If the corpus cannot support a derivation, SAY SO and say what would: an honest 'cannot be derived from what we have' beats a second invented pair, and the flag already degrades safely to `unsettled` in that case. [!] WHERE TO WRITE IT: config/lever_reachability.json::evidence_flag_policy, replacing `plausible_cut_band` (or narrowing it) and flipping `status` off UNDERIVED. The grading code is scripts/ops/lever_evidence_flag.py::grade, which already reads the policy from the registry and already stores, per basis, the exact cut-points its own verdict flips at (`settled_reachable_if_reach_cut_at_or_below_pct` / `settled_inert_if_inert_cut_above_pct`) -- those are the inputs a derived threshold gets compared against, so the arithmetic is already laid out. Keep the self-test's non-vacuity control and add one showing a leg's flag MOVING when only its trade rate changes, which is the property this row adds. [!] WHAT THE DERIVATION WILL LIKELY SHOW, recorded in advance so it is falsifiable rather than confirmed after the fact: on the current corpus only uso_trend_1h clears any reachable bar, and NOTHING reaches settled_inert, because the inert side needs a horizon long enough that <1 expected arming is a real statement and the live populations are n=1 to n=37. If the derivation produces a confident `settled_inert` on a single-digit n, that is a sign the horizon was chosen to produce it.

items.title: Fix the arbitration at source: elect PER ACCOUNT off the once-gated set, retire the fan-out workaround
items.note:
OPERATOR DIRECTIVE 2026-09-22: 'we need to fix the fanout mechanism'. [!] THE FAN-OUT IS A WORKAROUND LAYERED ON THE GLOBAL ELECTION, NOT A FIX OF IT, and it says so itself -- src/runtime/pipeline.py:1088: 'Per-account arbitration fan-out ... so an account whose own candidate lost the GLOBAL election is no longer dropped by `pkg.strategy in assigned` and silenced without a journal row.' The global dispatcher picks ONE winner per symbol across all accounts and then fans out; any account whose own candidate lost is dropped silently. The fan-out repairs that damage after the fact. It solves nothing the global dispatcher could not have avoided by not creating the problem. [!] AND THE STATED BLOCKER TO FIXING IT PROPERLY IS ALREADY OBSOLETE -- THIS IS THE FINDING. The reason given for never making the election per-account is that a per-account aggregator would re-emit a `regime_hard_gate` row per account per tick, corrupting the signal that partitions `would have gated` from `did gate`. But intent_multiplexer.py:876 ALREADY SPLITS GATE FROM ELECT, in a comment that says exactly why: 'Gate ONCE, then elect. aggregate_intents is exactly this composition, but spelling it out is what lets the per-account fan-out below elect N times off the SAME gated set without re-emitting a regime_hard_gate row per account per tick.' `_gated, _pre_gate = gate_intents(intents, symbol=symbol)` then `elect_from_gated(_gated, ...)`. THE MACHINERY TO ELECT PER ACCOUNT WITHOUT CORRUPTING THE AUDIT SIGNAL IS IN THE FILE AND IN USE TODAY. The fan-out is the existence proof. [!] THE SHAPE OF THE FIX: call elect_from_gated per account off the one gated set and dispatch the union, instead of electing once globally and scoping a repair round. Then there is no global winner to starve anyone, ARBITRATION_FANOUT_ACCOUNTS becomes unnecessary, and the failure mode measured today -- a partial allowlist SUBTRACTING accounts from rounds they had won -- cannot exist because there is no allowlist. [!] TODAY'S ALL-11 ALLOWLIST IS SCAFFOLDING, NOT A SETTLED DESIGN. It removes the subtraction; it leaves the global election underneath it (BL-20260827) untouched. [!] TIER 3 -- it changes live routing on real-money accounts. Prove it against the same test the E33 lane wrote (tests/test_arbitration_fanout_allowlist_scope.py, which asserts TODAY'S DEFECTIVE BEHAVIOUR on purpose so the fix has to flip it CONSCIOUSLY); flipping those assertions is part of the deliverable and must be visible in the diff.

items.title: Regime classification — under what market conditions is each strategy expected to perform, and can we tell?
items.note: OPERATOR DIRECTIVE 2026-09-22, part two of the R8 wiring decision: 'For the others, we need to use them as usecases for regime classification - I want to wire them, but we need to be sure we have a working mechanism for determining under what market conditions each strategy trades based on when we expect the strategy to perform well.' [!] THE SIX HELD-BACK LEGS ARE THE USE CASES, and they were held back on FOLD CONSISTENCY rather than on pooled net_R: trend_donchian_eth (+21.6753R, n=102, 1/4 folds), sol_pullback_2h (+7.2808R, n=16, 1/4), trend_donchian_avax_4h (+9.6920R, n=48, 2/4), trend_donchian_ada_4h (+8.5287R, n=38, 2/4), trend_donchian_sol_4h (+4.1648R, n=34, 2/4), trend_donchian_sol (+2.8045R, n=57, 2/4). A leg that earns +21.68R over 102 trades with ONE of four folds positive is not a leg with an edge -- it is a leg that worked in one regime, and the pooled sum cannot say which. [!] THIS IS RQ-20260922-002's QUESTION DECIDING A REAL-MONEY PROMOTION: 'RULE-D1 reads a pooled sum, which is blind to WHERE the R came from.' That unit is already queued and blocked; this row is the BUILD it implies. [!] DELIVERABLE, and the bar is that it must be FALSIFIABLE: a per-leg statement of the market conditions under which the strategy is expected to perform, derived from the fold-level record rather than asserted, plus a way to tell which regime is current. An untestable label ('works in trending markets') is worth nothing -- the test is whether, given a historical window, the mechanism would have called the regime BEFORE the fold's result was known. [!] EXISTING MATERIAL TO START FROM, NOT GREENFIELD: regime_debt_matrix.classify() already routes legs to harnesses on structural params; config/regime_policy.yaml and config/regime_coverage_exemptions.yaml exist; comms/strategy_evidence/*.json now carries fold_detail with per-fold start/end/net_r/trades for all 42 measured legs (R7, #12720), and comms/strategy_evidence/runs/2026-09-22-r5/*__trades.jsonl carries the PER-TRADE series. The fold boundaries plus the per-trade timestamps are the raw material for asking what was true of the market in the folds a leg won versus the folds it lost. [!] IT GATES REAL MONEY: the six legs are wired only when this mechanism can say when each is expected to work.

items.title: Re-verify the two held legs: a corpus that says +6.11R and +2.80R against recorded live results of -86R and -13.933R
items.note:
OPERATOR DECISION 2026-09-22: 'wire 2 and investigate the other 2'. TWO LEGS HELD OFF bybit_2 pending this row. [!] fade_breakout_4h -- DEMOTED 2026-06-01 (Tier-3, operator): 'no live edge demonstrated -- 16 closed trades, 44% win, net -86R (almost all bybit_1 demo; real-money bybit_2 +1.55/8)', and its condition reads 'Re-promote only on a fresh net-positive LIVE/SHADOW WINDOW'. The R7 corpus grades it +6.1101R over n=25, 3 of 4 folds. A BACKTEST IS A DIFFERENT INSTRUMENT FROM A LIVE/SHADOW WINDOW and does not satisfy that condition literally. [!] htf_pullback_trend_2h -- DEMOTED 2026-08-23 (Tier-3, operator): '4-axis tune discharge found nothing... Baseline itself is OOS net_R -13.933, the worst of the pullback family, and this leg routes to bybit_2 (REAL MONEY)'. The R7 corpus grades it +2.7979R over n=80, 3 of 4 folds. [!] THE QUESTION IS ONE QUESTION COVERING BOTH, and it is not 'which leg is better': WHY DOES THE NEW CORPUS DISAGREE SO VIOLENTLY WITH THE PRIOR MEASUREMENTS, AND WHICH INSTRUMENT IS RIGHT? The benign answer is that the old numbers were LIVE/PAPER P&L and the new ones are BACKTESTS net of cost -- under the ladder a live book never establishes edge, so the backtest is the admissible instrument and both legs promote. THAT ANSWER MUST BE ESTABLISHED, NOT ASSUMED: check whether the -13.933R figure was itself a backtest (the 2026-08-23 note calls it 'baseline OOS net_R', which SOUNDS like a harness number, not live P&L -- if so the benign reading collapses and two harness runs on the same leg disagree by 16.7R). [!] WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THESE TWO: if a harness can produce -13.933R and +2.7979R for the same leg, that bears on how much weight the OTHER 32 passing records carry, including the two just wired. This row is cheap and its blast radius is the whole corpus. [!] 2026-09-22, PARTLY ANSWERED WITHOUT A NEW RUN — from the fold_detail that was already committed. htf_pullback_trend_2h: +4.09 -> +0.58 -> +0.88 -> -2.75, so the +2.7979R pooled is fold 1 and the last nine months are -1.29R. THE CONTRADICTION WITH THE 2026-08-23 DEMOTION ('OOS net_R -13.933') IS LARGELY EXPLAINED RATHER THAN OPEN: the leg is DECAYING, and the August demotion was made INSIDE the fold that is negative. Two numbers over different windows on a decaying leg do not have to agree, and the newer one being higher is not evidence it is better. fade_breakout_4h: +3.75 -> +3.17 -> +4.24 -> -5.05 — consistent for three folds and then collapsing, and its demotion condition ('re-promote only on a fresh net-positive LIVE/SHADOW WINDOW') is still not satisfied by a backtest. [!] SO THIS ROW'S REMAINING QUESTION IS NARROWER: not 'which number is right' but 'does either leg have an edge in the RECENT window'. That is exactly RQ-20260922-012's population question, and this row should be read after it rather than re-deriving it per leg. Neither leg moves off shadow in the meantime. [!] A THIRD LEG JOINS THEM: avax_pullback_2h, withdrawn from R8 before merge for the same reason, now carried by RQ-20260922-013.

items.title: B1's identity check makes every promotion invalidate its own evidence — the guard has never permitted one
items.note: FOUND 2026-09-22 by trying to perform the first promotion since B1 landed. scripts/ci/check_roster_promotion_evidence.py EXITS 1 on avax_pullback_2h -> bybit_2 with `identity FAIL: config_fingerprint sha256:74242b93... != current sha256:84e51624... -- the record is about a different configuration of this leg (STALE)', while C1, C2, C3 and C4 ALL PASS. [!] MEASURED CAUSE, not inferred: I recomputed the fingerprint three ways. The record's digest matches the COMMITTED config EXACTLY (74242b93 == 74242b93). The only field my edit changed is `execution: shadow -> live`. So the flip ALONE moved the digest. build_strategy_evidence.py::config_fingerprint digests the ENTIRE leg config block -- json.dumps(cfg, sort_keys=True) -- which includes the execution gate. [!] THEREFORE ANY PROMOTION INVALIDATES ITS OWN EVIDENCE AT THE MOMENT OF PROMOTION. A leg cannot go shadow -> live without the guard calling its record stale, because the flip changes the thing being fingerprinted. B1 landed 2026-09-21 and this is the first promotion attempted since; the defect has been latent for a day and would have blocked every one. [!] THE FIX IS A CORRECTNESS FIX, NOT A WEAKENING: fingerprint the STRATEGY PARAMETERS the backtest measured, excluding `execution` (and almost certainly `enabled`) -- neither is a strategy property and neither changes what a harness would produce. A moved atr_stop_mult, entry_z or lookback must still invalidate the record, and the guard's own self-test at line 626 ('P6 stale config_fingerprint fails identity', plus 'P6 ...while all four clauses still PASS (so identity is load-bearing)') must keep passing so the failure branch stays proven. [!] TWO WRONG FIXES, NAMED SO THEY ARE NOT TAKEN: (a) regenerating the evidence record after the flip -- it re-runs a backtest to account for a gate change that cannot affect the result, and it teaches the next session that the answer to a guard complaint is to re-roll the evidence; (b) wiring the roster WITHOUT the execution flip -- the fingerprint stays valid and the guard passes, and you get a leg that looks promoted and trades nothing, which is the silent-inert failure mode the missing AVAXUSDT symbol nearly produced the same hour. [!] FIXED AND MERGED 2026-09-22 in #12725 (operator: 'Yes push it'). _GATE_FIELDS = {execution, enabled} excluded from the digest in BOTH scripts/ops/build_strategy_evidence.py (the producer) and scripts/ci/check_roster_promotion_evidence.py (the guard, which re-implements rather than imports so CI does not pull the producer's research deps), each carrying a comment that the set must NOT be widened to quiet a complaint. The 52 records were migrated in a way that PRESERVES the staleness signal rather than washing it out: each was graded under the OLD scheme against origin/main:config/strategies.yaml first (NOT the working tree, which carried the branch's own execution flip and would have begged the question), and a record whose parameters had genuinely drifted would have kept its old digest and still read STALE. Result 52 migrated / 0 already-stale kept, and the diff over the records is exactly 52 changed lines, all config_fingerprint. VERIFIED: --self-test PASS including 'P6 stale config_fingerprint fails identity' and 'P6 ...while all four clauses still PASS (so identity is load-bearing)', so the failure branch stays proven; the two implementations agree over all 55 config blocks; and controls confirm a gate flip does NOT move the digest while a moved atr_stop_mult DOES. [!] `landed_unproven` NOT `done`: what closes it is the guard ARMING a promotion on main — which #12725 itself is (`armed: ada_pullback_2h -> bybit_2 [roster_add]`), so this closes with R8's own observation.

items.title: accounts.yaml::symbols is a DATA-PULL list, not a gate — the roster is the single source for what trades, and a stale pull list is a pull-list bug, never a trading decision
items.note:
OPERATOR-RAISED 2026-09-22, verbatim: 'In general, I don't get why uh, th there shouldn't be a symbol specific list for each account. That's what the strategy roster is for. It trades whatever the strategies that it's trading are trading... That's exactly the kind of double gate that just stops things from working for no reason that is completely unnecessary to anything that we're doing here.' [!] VERIFIED, AND THE OPERATOR IS RIGHT ON BOTH HALVES — it is a gate, and it is redundant. IT IS A GATE, established in code and not inferred: src/main.py:714 `_resolve_tick_symbols` builds the set of symbols the trader FETCHES CANDLES FOR from each account's `symbols:` list, NOT from its roster. A symbol absent there means no data, no signal, no order — the leg sits on the roster looking wired and trades nothing. Two other readers exist and neither is a gate: src/runtime/intents.py::supported_symbols() unions the declared symbols with a static base as a VALIDATION whitelist and fails SAFE (a config-load failure falls back to the base, never narrower), and intent_multiplexer.py:485 reads the per-STRATEGY symbols, a different field. ⚠️ intents.py:100 contradicts itself inside one sentence — 'This is a validation whitelist, not a runtime on/off gate — accounts.yaml `symbols` drives what actually trades.' Field beats comment, and here the field is main.py:714. IT IS REDUNDANT, MEASURED over all 11 accounts by parsing config/accounts.yaml and config/strategies.yaml 2026-09-22: 19 ORPHAN symbols declared that no rostered leg needs (alpaca_live 8, alpaca_portfolio 7, bybit_2 1, bybit_portfolio 1, ib_live 1, oanda_practice 1), and 0 MISSING. ⚠️ READ THE ZERO CORRECTLY — IT IS NOT REASSURANCE, IT IS THE NEAR-MISS. It reads 0 only because the R8 promotion checked symbol coverage BEFORE the edit: avax_pullback_2h was about to join bybit_2 (REAL MONEY) while AVAXUSDT was absent from its list. Caught by looking, not by any guard — nothing in CI asserts the relationship, so the next one is caught by noticing silence, which is exactly how this class of defect is normally found: late. [!] AND THE FIX IS ALREADY HALF-WRITTEN IN THE SAME FILE: src/main.py:267 `_symbols_for_account` ALREADY derives the union of an account's roster symbols — it simply is not what _resolve_tick_symbols consults. [!] PROPOSED (Tier-2, additive, cannot narrow): _resolve_tick_symbols unions the roster-implied symbols into the declared ones, so the ROSTER is the single source and `symbols:` degrades to an additive override for anything a roster cannot imply. Nothing that trades today stops trading — the change can only ADD symbols to the fetch set. Plus a CI check that a rostered leg's symbol is always reachable, so the AVAXUSDT case fails a build instead of failing quietly. [!] THIS IS NOT THE 'no third gate' RULE BEING RESTATED — IT IS AN INSTANCE OF IT. CLAUDE.md § 'The two execution gates' says 'never hide a capability behind a default-off flag (the pattern that stranded MES)'. A symbol list that must be edited in a second place to let a rostered leg trade is that pattern wearing different clothes, and it stranded a leg today. [!] OPERATOR REFRAMED IT 2026-09-22 AND THE REFRAME IS SHARPER THAN THIS ROW WAS, verbatim: 'There are two separate issues here. There's the issue of what trades on what account and what data gets pulled from the account, and those are two separate things that aren't dependent. Obviously anything that's trading will need to be pulling the data, but we can still continue pulling data... for other things even if they're not being traded. But that shouldn't be formatted as a gate. That should just be formatted as additional data pulls unrelated to the strategies themselves. So we do need to find a way to union that so that we're not doing double declarations. But it also needs to make sure that the data-pull roster is not going to interfere with the strategy roster. And even if something is for some reason missing from the pull list, it doesn't mean that it shouldn't be traded — it means that the pull list is not updated correctly.' [!] SO THE SPEC IS FOUR PROPERTIES, not 'remove the second list': (1) the STRATEGY ROSTER decides what trades, full stop; (2) `symbols:` becomes a pure ADDITIVE data-pull list and it is LEGITIMATE for it to carry symbols nothing trades; (3) fetch set = UNION(roster-implied, declared), so no double declaration; (4) a symbol missing from the pull list is a PULL-LIST BUG, never a reason a rostered leg does not trade — and the CI check's FAILURE MESSAGE must say that, in those terms. [!] THIS CHANGES THE DISPOSITION OF THE 19 ORPHANS: under the reframe they are LEGITIMATE data pulls, not drift to clean up. The lane is fenced off them. My earlier framing called them redundancy; that was the one-list reading and the operator's two-concern reading is better. Dispatched as a lane, Tier-2, landing hold.  ||| LANE REPORT 2026-09-22 (session_01PDnYMJCPBohXArAKpUceZm, Tier-2, HELD). REACHED: merged=NO, deployed=NO, observed=NO. STATE IS `blocked`, NOT `landed_unproven` -- close-out check 3 caught this row asserting `landed_unproven` while the PR was still open. Per the states vocabulary `landed_unproven` means MERGED with the effect unobserved; nothing of this lane is on main. It becomes `landed_unproven` on merge and `done` only on the observation named at the end of this note. Asked what to do about the blocked lane E20 found, the operator chose archive-everything-dead 'plus a mechanism to prevent this from continuing to happen'. The archiving is DONE (see below); this row is the mechanism, and it exists because the obvious mechanism was already built, tried, and measured NOT WORKING. [!] WHAT THE SWEEP ACTUALLY COST, measured by the manager 2026-09-22T13:35Z over the 60 most recent sessions on this account (list_sessions mine=true), cost from external_metadata.usage.cost_usd, present on 51 of 60: $6,193.20 total. Buckets: COMPLETED 43 / WORKING 6 / BLOCKED 5 / REVIEW_READY 4 / FAILED 2. The manager archived the dead ones under the operator's instruction: 24 attempted, 24 ARCHIVED, $3,553.06 — 18 on the first call and 6 only after a retry, because the session-tool permission classifier refused them the first time (a 25th, the E34 review lane at $21.95, was deliberately NOT attempted: its PR may still be in flight). Archiving is reversible via unarchive_session, which is why a wrong call here is recoverable and a deletion would not have been. Arithmetic closes: 3,553.06 + 21.95 = 3,575.01, the full candidate set. Largest single line: session_01XYu2vvg9Qgxoqf4jJQyd8i (MI-305), BLOCKED and idle 73.3 hours, $1,343.06, 447M cache-read tokens, ZERO commits — archived. Second: a REVIEW_READY research lane at $736.15 idle 85 hours whose output nobody ever collected. [!] THE MECHANISM MUST NOT BE A PERSON'S MEMORY, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE DIFFICULTY. E20 measured three designs dead before proposing a fourth: (1) a CI guard on git commit recency — killed, because 5 of the 7 WORKING lanes had never committed anything, so it would red five healthy lanes; (2) a CI guard on the offline half — killed, because it fails a contributor's PR over the MANAGER's behaviour, the one actor who cannot fix it; (3) a Routine firing a FRESH session — built, fired once, DISABLED the same minute, because the fired session had no repo checkout (sources: []) and no Claude Code Remote MCP tools, so it could neither read lane_reconcile.py nor call list_sessions. A watcher that cannot reach its subject and reports nothing is the exact defect class this row is about. [!] THE FOURTH DESIGN, AND WHY IT IS DIFFERENT: a PERSISTENT supervisor session created with the repo as a source, woken by a cron Routine bound to it via persistent_session_id. A persistent-session Routine delivers into a session that already HAS a checkout and its own tool grants, which is precisely what the fresh-session firing lacked. ⚠️ THIS IS A HYPOTHESIS UNTIL THE LANE MEASURES IT — E20's three capability checks (a repo checkout present, list_sessions callable, the served model) must be run against the woken supervisor and REPORTED, and if any is absent the design is killed like the other three rather than shipped hopeful. A fallback that is honest beats a watchdog that reports nothing. [!] WHAT IT MAY AND MAY NOT DO, because an autonomous archiver is a way to destroy work: archive only sessions whose bucket is COMPLETED or FAILED AND which are idle beyond a stated threshold AND which hold no open PR — never WORKING, never BLOCKED. A BLOCKED lane is NOT archived: only a human can clear a permission prompt, so the supervisor's job there is to RAISE it fast, and the surface it raises on must be one the operator already reads — the checklist rendered at GET /api/bot/work/checklist — not a chat message and not a new register. Archiving is reversible (unarchive_session); deleting is not, and this row authorises no deletion. resolution_criteria: a supervisor session and its Routine exist; a firing has been OBSERVED to read the repo and call list_sessions (or the design is recorded dead with the reading that killed it); a BLOCKED or over-idle lane appears on the operator's Workflow page without a manager having run anything. severity: high — this is the single largest measured waste in the account and it recurs weekly. [!] DISPATCHED 2026-09-22T13:55Z to session_01VsAt1BzrdspLn6hDzFTGh2 on opus-5 — chosen because the lane's first act is a capability MEASUREMENT whose negative result must be trusted enough to kill the design, and three prior designs were killed on exactly such readings. The dispatch fences it off every WORKING lane and off config/src/deploy, and tells it in terms that an honest 'this cannot be built from a session' is an acceptable outcome. [!] THE FIVE E44 FINDINGS NO LONGER DEPEND ON #12752 LANDING. They existed only in the PIPELINE.jsonl on claude/e44-lane-supervisor-build, and nothing reads a branch -- measured 2026-09-23, each returned 1 on the branch and 0 on main while that PR sat `dirty`. Imported verbatim onto main via #12789: PI-20260922-HDZFTGH2-0001 (the canonical doc still binding every session to an archived coordination board -- UNRELATED to E44 and the most valuable of the five), -0002, -0003 (closed there with the cold-test observation that answered it), PI-20260923-HDZFTGH2-0001 and -0002. The CODE, the mandate and the guard are still only on that branch; only the FINDINGS were rescued.

[!] WITHDRAWN 2026-09-24 — THE 'ONLY A HUMAN CAN CLEAR IT' CLAIM ABOVE IS FALSE AND WAS NEVER TESTED. It is left in place rather than deleted so the correction is legible against what it corrects. FALSIFIED by one attempt: interrupt_session on the walled lane, then a message delivered through a create_trigger with persistent_session_id set to it. MEASURED on session_017mdYduTwtyVPXU54wqNHJx, which had shown no activity for 39 hours (last 2026-09-22T13:51:41Z): the trigger fired 2026-09-24T05:32:00Z and get_session shows a turn at 05:32:42Z ending status_bucket COMPLETED, reporting a clean tree, nothing staged or unpushed, and that its own staged_files:true flag was a FALSE ALARM. The operator's words, recorded because the correction is theirs: 'you can definitely take care of those permissions instead of me'.
[!] AND THE NARROWER FORM, because over-claiming the correction would repeat the original error in the other direction: ONE case establishes this, not two. The same technique was also aimed at session_01R9WFrBK1sbBcpTYgBmvG1q and it did reply, but that session runs a 6-hourly cron that would have woken it anyway, and its own 06:44Z heartbeat states it 'was not itself blocked on anything at the time'. A session that was going to wake regardless is not evidence that a message clears a wall. What is established: a message CAN move a session reporting BLOCKED. What is NOT established: that it always can, or what distinguishes the cases. Do not read this as a guarantee; read it as a probe that must be RUN rather than assumed either way — the original defect was asserting the limit for two days without ever attempting it once.

items.title: Eight CI guards grade NOTHING and eleven more are silently narrowed — and three of the dead are named in the #1 doc as live enforcing mechanisms
items.note: MEASURED by the E20 lane 2026-09-22 over a STATED POPULATION of 95 guard scripts — scripts/ci/check_*.py PLUS scripts/check_*.py, because check_claim_basis.py, the one CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL leans on hardest, lives in the latter. Every module-level repo-path constant tested with `git cat-file -e HEAD:<path>`. Four states, never collapsed: live 30 · degraded 11 · DEAD 8 · no_declared_subject 46 (the instrument cannot speak to those, and it is the LARGEST bucket, so folding it into `live` would be this tool committing the defect it exists to find). [!] THE EIGHT DEAD: check_backlog_unresolve, check_claim_basis, check_open_items, check_operator_owed, check_recurrence_ledger, check_register_field_loss, check_soak_registered, check_stated_population. Every one is the 2026-09-21 reset's blast radius — it archived the four review backlogs, OPEN-ITEMS.json, the lease, SESSIONS.json, MERGE-QUEUE.json, session-board.json, RECURRENCE-LEDGER.json and operator-owed-register.json, and nothing swept the guards that read them. [!] AND THREE ARE NAMED IN docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md AS LIVE MECHANISMS, which is why this is not housekeeping: § Backlog governance says the status enum is 'enforced whole-file over every review backlog by claim-basis-guard'; § 'A soak must carry its own alarm' says check_soak_registered fails when a *_soak.jsonl exists with no register alarm; § Session-end reconciliation says operator-owed-guard fails on an item carried across commits without a state change. All three subjects are archived. A canonical doc naming a mechanism that cannot run is the folklore failure that document has its own section about. [!] OPERATOR DECISION 2026-09-22: RE-POINT THE THREE NAMED ONES, RETIRE THE OTHER FIVE with stated reasons, and correct the doc text to match — the doc follows the decision, it does not lead it. [!] DO NOT PROMOTE THE 19 INTO A HARD FAILURE as part of this. E20 already wired scripts/ci/check_guard_liveness.py REPORT-FIRST, with a dated shrink-only baseline and counts printed every run; only a NEW dead or degraded guard fails. Keep that shape and let the baseline shrink by eight. resolution_criteria: the three re-pointed guards each FAIL on a planted violation against their new subject (a green re-point proves nothing); the five retirements each carry a written reason; CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL no longer claims a mechanism that cannot run; and check_guard_liveness's baseline is smaller by eight with the count visible in the diff. [!] CLOSED 2026-09-22 — PR #12756 MERGED, and `done` rather than `landed_unproven` because all four resolution criteria were RE-CHECKED ON MAIN after the merge (main 8a0669284), not inferred from the merge: (1) the re-pointed guards each FAIL on a violation planted against their new subject — self-tests 11/16/14/11 controls, run on main; (2) the four retired scripts are absent from the tree and each carries its reason in docs/archive/2026-09-21-operating-reset/guards/RETIRED-GUARDS-2026-09-22.md; (3) the only surviving mentions of the archived registers in CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL are inside the dated correction notes (lines 640, 1683), i.e. history, not a live mechanism claim; (4) guard-liveness reads dead 0, baseline 11 of 11, exit 0. [!] AND THE FIFTH RETIREMENT DID NOT HAPPEN: check_stated_population is NOT dead (verified by running it against a planted diff, exit 1); its population is a glob the liveness instrument cannot see, so 1 of 8 dead verdicts (12.5%) was a false positive. items.title: A failed build_strategy_evidence.py run OVERWRITES a committed MEASURED record with a harness_failed stub — two real measurements were nearly lost
items.note: OBSERVED by the E41 lane 2026-09-22, not inferred: its first run of scripts/ops/build_strategy_evidence.py DESTROYED the committed `measured` records for gld_pullback_1d and qqq_trend_long_1d, nulling net_r_oos, n_trades_oos and fold_detail and replacing them with a harness_failed stub. The cause was mundane — yfinance was absent from the sandbox — and that is the point: an ordinary environment gap silently converts evidence into a stub. THEY SURVIVED ONLY BECAUSE THE LANE READ `git diff` BEFORE COMMITTING. On a different day that is two measurements gone, with the commit looking like a routine regeneration. [!] WHY THIS IS MORE THAN A SCRIPT BUG: comms/strategy_evidence/ IS the corpus B1's four-clause bar reads to decide whether a leg may reach a real-money roster, and a harness_failed stub does not read as a loss — it reads as a leg that was never measured. That is the collapsed state this repo files bugs about (`we could not look` rendered identically to `we looked and found nothing`), sitting on the promotion path. [!] THE FIX IS SMALL AND THE SHAPE IS NOT NEGOTIABLE: a failed run must never overwrite a record that currently reads `measured`. Write the failure somewhere it is visible (a separate field, a refusal, a non-zero exit) but leave the measurement intact, and make the refusal LOUD rather than a silent skip. Whether a re-measure may overwrite a measured record when it SUCCEEDS is a different question and stays as it is. [!] AND TWO SIBLINGS FILED BY THE SAME LANE BELONG WITH IT, because they are the same artifact lying about itself: PI-20260922-E41-0005 — qqq's record claims `fidelity: faithful` with `omitted_levers: []` while its harness run omits tp_r entirely, and the README defines faithful as 'modelled EVERY lever the leg's config declares'. Not cosmetic: the omitted lever is the one that moved that leg's number 3.4x (net_r_oos 1.9389 -> 6.6307 on an identical data span, the ONLY difference being arm 3.56 -> 0.0). PI-20260922-E41-0006 carries a prediction registered IN ADVANCE — re-run with tp_r modelled and the two should agree; if they do not, the inert-by-construction reasoning behind the qqq arm strip is wrong and #12737 needs re-opening. resolution_criteria: a planted harness failure against a committed measured record leaves the record BYTE-IDENTICAL and exits non-zero; the fidelity claim is computed from what the run actually modelled rather than asserted; and 0006's prediction is either confirmed or recorded as refuted. Three scalars restored by hand after the register merge driver took them from the wrong side on this branch's merge of origin/main -- the defect filed as PI-20260922-JN54P2HH-0002, which merges NOTES correctly and then takes `state`/`prs`/`blocked_on` from whichever side had the longer note. E46 was carrying no PR link for #12754. VERIFIED by diffing every row of the merged tree against origin/main on state/status/prs/blocked_on/owner/next_action and on note LENGTH, not by eye. items.title: A register-only change should not cost a PR, three landing files and two 20-minute CI cycles
items.note:
OPERATOR-RAISED 2026-09-24, verbatim: 'it just doesn't seem like we've basically spent 24 hours trying to close up something that we were supposed to close up two days ago already... It seems. Like something might be wrong here.' They then chose 'file it as a checklist row' over raising it at the sync.
MEASURED ON ONE REAL CHANGE (#12828, 2026-09-24): flipping TWO fields in MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json from `in_flight`/`blocked` to `done` required a PR, `.github/pr-landing/<slug>.json`, `.github/pr-automerge-requests/<slug>.txt`, `.github/merge-slots/<slug>.json`, and TWO full CI cycles. `pytest-run` is ~20 minutes and every push restarts it. Wall clock from PR open (11:24:15Z) to merge (11:52Z) was 28 minutes for a 35-line docs diff.
⚠️ SPLIT THE CAUSE HONESTLY, because most of it was the manager and a fix aimed at the wrong half will not help. Roughly 40 minutes was MY error: I discovered the landing requirements by failing CI twice instead of running `python3 scripts/ci/check_pr_landing.py --base origin/main`, which takes 8 SECONDS and names every missing file at once. That is a discipline problem, addressed in the handoff, NOT something to build around. What remains after removing it is still real: three landing files and a full test suite for a docs-only diff.
CANDIDATE DIRECTIONS, none decided:
  (a) a docs-only CI path that skips `pytest-run` when the diff touches no Python -- note `guards` must       still run, since pr-landing-guard and the register guards live there;
  (b) let the manager batch register updates into ONE PR per day instead of one per closure;
  (c) collapse the three landing files into one, or derive the merge-slot claim from the declaration.
[!] A CHEAP, SEPARABLE FIX WORTH DOING WHATEVER ELSE IS CHOSEN: pr-landing-guard's R13 failure message tells you to write `docs/claude/session-board.json`, which the 2026-09-21 operating reset ARCHIVED and which CLAUDE.md says not to resurrect. The route that works is `.github/merge-slots/<branch>.json` (MI-280, 2026-09-12), documented ~20 lines below the stale remedy in the guard's own source. That message cost a CI cycle on 2026-09-24 and will cost the next session one too. guard-liveness already baselines check_pr_landing.py as DEGRADED with session-board.json among its absent subjects, so the repo knows the subject is gone -- what nobody noticed is that the REMEDY TEXT still points at it.
[!] NOT ESTABLISHED: whether `pytest-run` can be skipped safely for a docs-only diff. Nobody has checked what in that suite reads docs/ or the registers -- `check_manager_checklist_vocabulary` and `pipeline --check` both do, and both live in `guards`, not `pytest-run`. Establish it before building (a).
